# @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework

## 0.396.0

### Minor Changes

- dd12c0d: Entity update, delete, restore and forget now answer not_found for a row the caller cannot read, including a join row whose parentRef host the caller cannot read.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Entity writes on a row the caller cannot read fail with not_found
  detail: update, delete, restore and forget only checked access.write, so on an entity with an owner access.read rule and no access.write any tenant member with handler access could change or delete another member's row, and delete returned the decrypted row. They now apply the same access.read rule and parentRef host-visibility gate as detail and answer not_found, so the row's existence stays hidden. Framework system writes are exempt. A write the caller could not read but that failed the write rule before now reports not_found instead of ownership_denied.
  migration: Writes on rows the caller cannot read now fail with not_found; give such writers read access or run them as system. Custom handlers that call the executor directly get the parentRef gate by passing parentVisibility: { entities: ctx.registry.getAllEntities() }, as the generated handlers do.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- Updated dependencies [dd12c0d]
  - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types@0.396.0

## 0.395.0

### Patch Changes

- 373a722: A file upload with a revoked or expired session sends the user to the login with the session-ended banner.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: A file upload with an ended session ends up at the login
  detail: POST /files answered an anonymous caller (revoked or expired session) with 403 forbidden or a validation error, so the browser showed an upload error instead of the login. Anonymous callers can never use an upload (they cannot bind pending files), so every upload without a session now answers 401 with code unauthenticated before the body is read, and the file upload fields signal the ended session like any other request. Signed-in callers without permission still get 403.
  -->
- Updated dependencies [6599341]
  - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types@0.395.0

## 0.394.0

### Minor Changes

- a91f814: New `events prune` command removes whole aggregate types from the event log.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: events prune removes retired aggregate types from the event log
  detail: `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/events-cli` exports `runEventsCli(argv, out, { features, rowLevelSecurity? })`. `events prune --aggregate-type <type> [--aggregate-type <type> ...]` reports events, aggregates and tenants per type; with `--apply` it deletes, in one transaction and in system scope, the events, snapshots, archive markers and dead letters of these types and empties the projections fed only by them. A projection that also reads other types makes the run refuse. Unknown or empty types fail without deleting anything. Use it when old events of a retired type break the rebuild of `schema apply`. Apps add `if (cmd === "events")` to `bin/kumiko.ts`; new scaffolds get it.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: improvement
  title: Scaffolded bin/kumiko.ts dispatches events
  detail: The generated standalone CLI now forwards `events` to `runEventsCli` with the app's features and row level security mode.
  -->
- 9638cd4: Per-call upload limit, a handler-side file read check, nested-safe `beforeTransaction`, and a catch-up boot rule.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: files
  type: improvement
  title: createFileRefFromBytes takes a per-call maxSize
  detail: `CreateFileRefInput.maxSize` (bytes) replaces the route default for that call, so server-side generated files such as mail attachments can exceed the 10 MB upload default without raising it for browsers. A file field's own maxSize still applies first. `configuredMaxUploadBytes(registry)` returns the configured route limit in bytes, or undefined.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: files
  type: improvement
  title: canCallerReadFileRef answers the file read decision in handlers
  detail: `canCallerReadFileRef(ctx, fileRef)` applies the same rule as GET /files/:id: the configured accessGuard, otherwise the default guard with the configured privilegedRoles and the bound record's detail query. `createDefaultGuard` is exported from the files barrel. A handler that lists or links files no longer needs its own copy of the rule.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: beforeTransactionWhenNested skip lets a handler with a beforeTransaction phase run nested
  detail: `beforeTransactionWhenNested: "skip"` on a write handler lets a nested ctx.dispatch.write run it without the phase. `event.prepared` is then `undefined` (typed `TPrepared | undefined`) and the handler does that work inside its own transaction. Top-level commands still run the phase. Without the option a nested call stays rejected. Boot rejects the option without beforeTransaction and together with reserveBeforeTransaction; transaction "perCommand" is already rejected next to beforeTransaction.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: jobs
  type: fix
  title: catchUp job consumers ignore foreign event types before upcasting, and catchUp with maxPerTenant skip fails at boot
  detail: A catch-up job consumer now filters on the trigger's event types before the stored event is upcast, so a foreign event with a failing upcaster no longer stalls the job cursor. Boot rejects `trigger.catchUp` together with `maxPerTenant` onLimit "skip" (including the number shorthand): a replay must not discard history. Use onLimit "defer".
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: files
  type: improvement
  title: Projection entities are server-side attach targets for files
  detail: An entity declared on a projection (r.projection with entity) is a read-model entity: a files field on it can be the attachTo target of createFileRefFromBytes and uploadFileBytesBeforeTransaction, and the file read check uses the owning feature's `<name>:detail` query for it. The registry gets getReadModelEntity and getReadModelEntityOwner; two projections declaring an entity for the same source fail the boot. POST /files still accepts only r.entity targets, so a client can never attach to a read model. deleteFileRefsBoundToRecord soft-deletes the fileRefs of one record for owners that remove it without an r.entity delete.
  -->
- 9c4e277: Imported mails keep their full text, the original and their attachments. A mail the provider cannot parse no longer blocks a mailbox, a mailbox that stops syncing says so, a disconnected mailbox can come back without duplicates, and a new or reactivated mailbox syncs right away.

  feature: inbound-mail-foundation
  type: improvement
  title: Imported mails store full text, original and attachments
  detail: ingest-message now takes bodyText (at most 32,000 characters, cut with bodyTextTruncated set; 32,000 keeps a long mail readable while one event, one projection row and the PII-encrypted column stay small, the original keeps everything), rawMime, bodyHtml, attachments (at most 50) and skippedAttachments (at most 200). The original is stored as .eml (or .html for HTML-only mails) and each attachment as a file reference through file storage; apps without a file provider still import the mail, mark contentState unavailable and show the mailbox as interrupted. The event inbound-message-received is now v2 with an upcast that defaults the new fields; bodyText is personal tenant data. The new query inbound-mail-foundation:query:message:content returns text, original reference and attachments of one mail; message:list never carries the body. Retention removes the mail row, its body object and its attachment files. RawInboundMessage gains text, html, attachments and skippedAttachments.
  -->

The new plugin method fetchContent reloads the content of a mail by provider id.

The account list shows quarantinedCount and lastError, the new handler acknowledge-quarantine confirms the entries, acknowledged entries are purged by retention after 90 days, and the tenant-destroy hook removes them.

- d24b405: Inbound mail with configurable roles and private personal mailboxes
  
  `createInboundMailFoundationFeature` and `createInboundProviderImapFeature` take `{ userRoles, adminRoles }` (defaults `User` and `TenantAdmin`/`SystemAdmin`); a boot check rejects deviating options. The mail of a personal mailbox (messages, body, attachments, quarantine) is now readable by its owner only, not by admins; admins still see the account metadata and manage shared mailboxes. The owner reactivates a personal IMAP mailbox in the new "My mailboxes" flow. The content-fetched event is version 3 and carries `accountId` and `ownerUserId` (null for older events). `EntityDefinition.attachedFileAccess: "record-only"` keeps the files privileged roles from reading or deleting attached files, and `createDefaultGuard` takes the matching fourth parameter. `SendMailFromAccountContext.dispatch` is query-only. A live list now resyncs on every stream open and an infinity list adopts a refresh that lands during its first load.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: inbound-mail-foundation
  type: breaking
  title: Personal mail is private to its owner, roles are configurable
  detail: Admins no longer read messages, bodies, attachments or quarantine of a personal mailbox; list-accounts still shows them the account without counts. The screens and the IMAP handlers are factories (createMailAccountListScreen, createImapConnectScreen and others) taking the resolved roles instead of constants. The content-fetched event is version 3 with accountId and ownerUserId. createDefaultGuard has a fourth parameter recordOnlyEntityTypes; for those entity types the files privilegedRoles no longer read or delete attached files (shared mailboxes included), only the uploader and readers of the record do. The OAuth connect route answers 403 mail_role_required to callers without a mail role.
  migration: |
    Apps that import mailAccountListScreen, mailAccountEditScreen, mailAccountSenderCheckScreen, myMailAccountListScreen, mailQuarantineScreen, imapConnectScreen or imapReconnectScreen call the matching create*Screen factory with resolveInboundMailRoles(). Apps with their own roles pass { userRoles, adminRoles } to createInboundMailFoundationFeature and the same options to createInboundProviderImapFeature. Callers of createDefaultGuard pass a Set of record-only entity types as fourth argument. Code that read personal mail as an admin must run as the owner; the nullable accountId and ownerUserId on content-fetched events need no action.
  -->
- 9638cd4: A failing PII key store raises its own error instead of a generic one.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: KMS outages surface as EncryptionUnavailableError

Key-state errors (KeyNotFoundError, KeyErasedError, KeyAlreadyExistsError) keep their types. Callers can tell an outage, which they retry later, from a problem with the record.
  -->
- a91f814: Dashboards can embed a projectionDetail as a screen panel, list toolbar actions can be gated with `visibleWhen`, a screen `fallback` can pick its screen by failure reason, and the live-signal entity name now comes from one shared `toKebab`. All additions are optional.

  -->

Boot checks the query, its output field and that it needs no input. relatedList toolbar actions reject `visibleWhen`.

Boot now fails when two entities of different features fold to the same key (`billing.period` and `billingPeriod`), instead of merging their read rules.

- 99eea8a: requiredEnvFor reads a required env var in ops scripts
  
  @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/env exports requiredEnvFor(label, env). It returns a reader that hands back the value of a set variable and throws "[label] required env var NAME is missing or empty" otherwise; an empty string counts as missing and the error never contains a value. The env source is passed in, so a script can read from the KEK-resolved env of resolvePlatformKeks as well as from process.env. It replaces the requiredEnv copies in app bin/ops scripts.

  feature: framework

  title: requiredEnvFor reads a required env var in ops scripts
  -->

- 383b6a8: The field-to-column mapping, the entity index set and the migration SQL rendering are split into smaller steps without changing any generated table or migration.

  feature: framework

- c639de3: Two new guards: `test-title` flags German or issue-referencing test titles, and `ignore-tag-reason` flags `kumiko-lint-ignore` tags without a real reason. The comment-language guard no longer flags names like "Müller GmbH" or "Zürich".
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement
  title: New test-title and ignore-tag-reason guards, fewer comment-language false positives
  detail: test-title scans test, it and describe titles (including each/skip/only chains) for German text (an umlaut, two German function words, or one unambiguous German word) and issue references. ignore-tag-reason requires a kumiko-lint-ignore reason of at least three words that is not generic. Both start with a baseline of 0 and warn only in repos without a baseline. The comment-language guard now reports a comment only when a lowercase word contains an umlaut, an umlaut appears together with a German function word, or at least two German markers appear, so proper nouns with umlauts pass.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 8e6d41e: The stream-tenant backfill no longer fails on two membership streams of one (user, tenant) pair, `seedTenantMembership` no longer starts such a second stream, and replicas booting at the same time no longer race on creating `kumiko_es_operations`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant
  type: fix
  title: The stream-tenant backfill archives membership streams a projection replay must not see
  detail: Before the membership projection is rebuilt, the backfill reads the membership lifecycle from the event log and archives two kinds of streams. Streams of a user whose every stream is archived are archived with it, so a rebuild does not bring back memberships of users that no longer exist. When a second stream of a (userId, tenantId) pair was created while another one was still alive, the stream with the newest event stays and the others are archived; a pair that was removed and added again is left alone. Before, the rebuild failed on read_tenant_memberships_unique on every boot and the backfill stayed pending. The archived streams are logged as a warning and returned in membershipStreamsArchived. If a collision still remains, the failure says so and the step runs again on the next boot. Membership rows of archived users disappear from read_tenant_memberships with the rebuild.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant
  type: fix
  title: seedTenantMembership reuses the live membership stream of a pair
  detail: seedTenantMembership looked only at read_tenant_memberships. After the row was lost it created a second stream for the same pair, which made every later rebuild of the projection collide. It now also checks the event log and returns the id of the pair's live stream without writing anything. The seed does not bring the lost row back; only a rebuild of the membership projection does, and nothing triggers one on its own, so until then the user has no membership in that tenant.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Concurrent boots create kumiko_es_operations without a race
  detail: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is not race-safe in Postgres, so replicas booting against a fresh database could fail on pg_type_typname_nsp_index. createEsOperationsTable now takes an advisory lock and checks again before it creates the table.
  -->
- ffe0424: Cloudflare is removed from the platform sub-processor list.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Cloudflare is no longer listed as a sub-processor
  detail: DNS moved to Hetzner, so Cloudflare, Inc. no longer processes data for the platform. The entry is gone from KUMIKO_SUB_PROCESSORS, which means it is missing from /api/compliance/sub-processors and from the sub-processor RSS feed.
  -->

## 0.390.1

### Patch Changes

- 8297c01: `schema apply` in the production image heals the framework tables in the runtime's row-level security mode, plus follow-ups from the 0.390 bump: rebuild timestamp drift, scoped live check in `kumiko check`, codemod and upgrade fixes, zod and mailparser security ranges.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: schema apply in the production image uses the runtime's row-level security mode
  detail: The app image ships only kumiko/migrations, not kumiko/schema.ts. Without the schema file `schema apply` ran with row-level security "off", so kumiko_events, kumiko_snapshots and kumiko_archived_streams were not healed and the boot of an app in "on" mode (the default) failed with "framework tables without it". Without a schema file apply now uses the same default as runProdApp. RunSchemaCliOptions takes an optional rowLevelSecurity, which wins over the schema file; the scaffolded bin/kumiko.ts passes appConfig.rowLevelSecurity, like bin/main.ts does for runProdApp. Apps that do not set rowLevelSecurity need no change. An app that sets rowLevelSecurity "off" and keeps a hand-written bin/kumiko.ts must pass rowLevelSecurity: "off" to runSchemaCli, otherwise apply enables row-level security on the framework tables and the app's "off" boot check fails.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Projection rebuilds no longer report drift on timestamptz columns
  detail: Event payloads keep the microseconds of an instant, the live write stores milliseconds. A rebuild bound the payload's ISO string unchanged and wrote a different value, which the shadow diff reported as column drift. ISO instant strings bound to a timestamptz column are now truncated to milliseconds like Temporal.Instant values.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: The live row-level security check of `kumiko check` covers only the app's own tables
  detail: `schema validate` (the boot step of `kumiko check`) checks the live database when DATABASE_URL is set. On a dev database several apps share it failed on the other apps' tables. It now checks the tables kumiko/schema.ts declares plus the framework tables; tables no feature declares any more are still reported by the boot check, which runs against the app's own database. An unreachable database still fails the check.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: kumiko-upgrade runs the codemods of its own feature-ast install
  detail: The kumiko-upgrade bins of kumiko-cli and kumiko-dev-server now look for the codemod scripts from their own package first, so a feature-ast copy hoisted above the app (for example in a workspace parent) can no longer supply codemods of another version. runUpgradeCli takes an optional codemodResolveFrom for that; without it the search still starts at the repo root.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: feature-ast
  type: fix
  title: Codemods skip gitignored files, ctx-namespaces finds structural helpers across files
  detail: collectSourceFiles, used by the codemods, leaves out files the repository's .gitignore excludes, such as generated output and local worktrees. The ctx-namespaces codemod loads all files of a tsconfig project before rewriting, so a helper with a structural `{ query }` context type is migrated even when its handler caller sits in a file processed later.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: inbound-provider-imap
  type: fix
  title: mailparser moved to a version without known nodemailer advisories
  detail: mailparser moves to ^3.12.4, which pins nodemailer 10.2.1, so apps no longer get nodemailer 10.0.13 through it.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: zod range moved to ^4.6.7
  detail: All framework packages and the scaffold template require zod ^4.6.7, which fixes GHSA-MRHX-C7XC-M3W5.

- Updated dependencies [8297c01]
  - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types@0.390.1

## 0.390.0

### Minor Changes

- 5d7dfe1: HandlerContext drops the boot wiring: services, lifecycle and tenants replace the flat members, and hooks receive the HandlerContext.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: HandlerContext without wiring, hooks receive the HandlerContext
  codemod: scripts/codemod/ctx-namespaces.ts
  detail: HandlerContext has 19 members and no longer carries the AppContext wiring. ctx.services holds redis, cacheSync, jobRunner, searchAdapter, entityCache, secrets, kms, files, derivatives, configResolver, configEncryption, rateLimit, effectiveFeatures and masterKeyProvider; every key of an app's extraContext that the framework does not know now lives in ctx.services.extensions (it used to sit flat on the context through a spread, invisible to tsc). ctx.lifecycle holds afterCommit and afterRollback (replacing scheduleAfterCommit and scheduleAfterRollback), signal and runPreSave. ctx.tenants holds config (replacing configFor) and writeTarget (replacing forTenant). ctx.obs gains meter, and the flat log, tracer, _tenantId, systemUser and triggeredBy are gone; read ctx.user.tenantId and ctx.obs.log. JobContext no longer extends the shared wiring fields; it gets services and lifecycle.signal and keeps systemUser, triggeredBy and its job fields. All hooks (preSave, postSave, postSaveBatch, preDelete, postDelete, postDeleteBatch, preQuery, postQuery) and the system hook definitions receive the HandlerContext instead of the AppContext, and the batch hooks run on a real handler context built per flush. AppContext stays the flat boot wiring and declares services as never, so a handler or job context can no longer be passed to a function that takes an AppContext. The context of beforeTransaction no longer exposes ctx.systemDb.outsideTransaction, which was a hole next to the denied ctx.db.outsideTransaction. The member-resolution and pre-transaction contexts also drop the notify factories from ctx.services, and member resolution drops _fileProviderResolver, so neither can rebuild the denied notify or file storage. Helpers that took a structural context with an optional flat member read undefined once a handler context stopped carrying it; their shapes now make that a type error: requireSecretsContext, FileProviderContext (createFileProviderForTenant) and MailTransportContext (createTransportForTenant) take a required secrets key (handlers pass { secrets: ctx.services.secrets, user: ctx.user }), and CreateFileRefContext/UploadFileBytesContext read services.files, so a handler or job context passes straight in. bridgeStub accepts a services option.
  migration: |
    Run kumiko-upgrade --apply; it runs the ctx-namespaces codemod. It rewrites ctx.redis, cacheSync, jobRunner, searchAdapter, entityCache, secrets, kms, files, derivatives, configResolver, effectiveFeatures and the other service members to ctx.services.*, scheduleAfterCommit and scheduleAfterRollback to ctx.lifecycle.afterCommit and afterRollback, signal to ctx.lifecycle.signal, configFor and forTenant to ctx.tenants.config and writeTarget, and hook parameters annotated AppContext to HandlerContext, including context.log to context.obs.log in the hook body. Keys of your extraContext that you read through a cast move to ctx.services.extensions. Listed for manual review: ctx.systemUser, ctx.triggeredBy and ctx._tenantId on a HandlerContext (read ctx.user), a handler or job context passed to a function that takes an AppContext (narrow that parameter to the members it reads), spread literals next to moved members, and a handler or job context passed to a parameter whose structural type reads a moved member (it would read undefined without a type error). Hand-built test contexts take services, lifecycle and tenants from bridgeStub({ services }).
  -->
- a01d30a: HandlerContext and JobContext group their members into namespaces: db.outsideTransaction, events, dispatch, auth and obs.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: HandlerContext and JobContext use namespaces instead of flat members
  codemod: scripts/codemod/ctx-namespaces.ts
  detail: The roughly 40 flat members of HandlerContext are grouped by purpose, with no deprecated aliases. ctx.db.outsideTransaction replaces ctx.dbOutsideTransaction and ctx.outsideTransaction (the property is non-enumerable and sits on the same db object, so TenantDb identity stays intact; it is undefined in the member-resolution and before-transaction phases and in platform-metering tenant mode). ctx.events holds append, unsafeAppend, tryAppend, fetchForWriting, load, archive, restore, isArchived, snapshot and loadWithSnapshot. ctx.dispatch holds query, queryAs, write, writeAs, queryAsMember and queryProjection. ctx.auth holds resolveClaims and resolveActiveMembership. ctx.obs holds log, tracer, metrics and metricsFor, and ctx.obs.log is now always a Logger. JobContext gets the subsets events.append, dispatch.write/writeAs/queryAs/queryAsMember and obs.log/metricsFor. reserveBeforeTransaction and beforeTransaction receive the new ReservationContext and BeforeTransactionContext types, so the surfaces they deny no longer exist on the type. The deprecated _configAccessorFactory alias is removed; use configAccessorFactory. The cap-counter resolvers and the template-resolver PrepareContext now take ReservationContext instead of HandlerContext (type-level break for callers passing a full HandlerContext-typed value to a narrower position, and for wrappers declaring the old type). attachOutsideTransaction(db, outsideDb) from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine gives hand-built contexts a db.outsideTransaction; it mutates the passed db with a non-enumerable property (Object.defineProperty) and returns the same object. bridgeStub now accepts log and dispatch options. AppContext stays flat, and the context handed to postSave, preDelete, postDelete and postQuery hooks still reads context.log; a separate hook context follows in a later release.
  migration: |
    Run kumiko-upgrade --apply; it runs the ctx-namespaces codemod. It rewrites ctx.dbOutsideTransaction and ctx.outsideTransaction to ctx.db.outsideTransaction, ctx.appendEvent/unsafeAppendEvent/tryAppendEvent/fetchForWriting/loadAggregate/archiveStream/restoreStream/isStreamArchived/snapshotAggregate/loadAggregateWithSnapshot to ctx.events.append/unsafeAppend/tryAppend/fetchForWriting/load/archive/restore/isArchived/snapshot/loadWithSnapshot, ctx.query/queryAs/write/writeAs/queryAsMember/queryProjection to ctx.dispatch.*, ctx.resolveAuthClaims/resolveActiveMembership to ctx.auth.resolveClaims/resolveActiveMembership, and ctx.log/tracer/metrics/metricsFor to ctx.obs.*. Object literals typed as HandlerContext or JobContext (test mocks) are nested the same way. Sites the codemod cannot resolve are listed for manual review: spread literals, untyped receivers, and AppContext reads such as context.log in hooks, which stay as they are. Manual pattern { db: someDb, dbOutsideTransaction: x } becomes db: attachOutsideTransaction(someDb, x). Spread calls such as ...bridgeStub() next to moved members are reworked by hand; pass log/dispatch as bridgeStub options. Rename _configAccessorFactory to configAccessorFactory where you set it on an AppContext.
  -->
- 454b49d: Feature AST, pattern library and codemods moved to the new package @cosmicdrift/kumiko-feature-ast; kumiko-upgrade heals stale open lines in CHANGELOG.md
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Feature AST, pattern library and codemods moved to @cosmicdrift/kumiko-feature-ast
  codemod: scripts/codemod/feature-ast-package.ts
  migration: |
    Import these names from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-feature-ast instead of @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine: AddEntityArgs, AddHookArgs, AddRelationArgs, AddWriteHandlerArgs, FeaturePatcher, FeaturePattern, FeaturePatternKind, FormFieldLabel, FormFieldSpec, FormInputType, HandlerHeaderUpdate, ParseError, ParseResult, PatternCategory, PatternChange, PatternChangeIssue, PatternChangesParseResult, PatternFormSchema, PatternId, RenderFeatureFileInput, SourceLocation, PATTERN_LIBRARY, VERSION_HEADER, addPattern, applyChanges, createFeaturePatcher, getPatternSchema, groupByCategory, parseFeatureFile, parsePatternChanges, parseSourceFile, removePattern, renderFeatureFile, renderPattern, replacePattern, updatePattern. Import CodemodOptions, CodemodReport, CodemodResult, FileAnalysis, ParsedHandlerInfo, analyzeFile, analyzeHandlerArrow, convertFile, generatePerformBlock, runCodemod, scanForCandidates from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-feature-ast/codemod instead of @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine/codemod. Add @cosmicdrift/kumiko-feature-ast to the dependencies of the importing package; the codemod does both. @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework no longer installs ts-morph.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: kumiko-upgrade --apply and --resolve heal stale open lines in CHANGELOG.md
  migration: |
    Every manual migration the upgrade marker lists as resolved gets its status in CHANGELOG.md, including `- [open]` lines in older sections left behind by a resolve with an older CLI.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: feature-ast
  type: improvement
  title: New package @cosmicdrift/kumiko-feature-ast
  -->
  
  The feature-file AST (parse, patch, render), the pattern library and the upgrade codemods now live in their own package, so the framework and its production images no longer carry ts-morph. The package publishes `.` and the Bun-only `./codemod`.
- be576a7: Jobs append their own events with `ctx.events.append`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Jobs append their own events with ctx.events.append
  detail: Jobs no longer need escapeHatch or unsafeRaw plus the low-level event-store API to append their own feature's events. The same ownership and schema rules apply as in write handlers, and the append runs in its own transaction together with the inline projections.
  migration: |
    JobContext has a new required field events.append. Code that builds a JobContext object by hand (boot seeds, test fixtures) and does not spread bridgeStub() adds an events.append that throws when the code under test never appends. Jobs that appended their own feature's events through escapeHatch or unsafeRaw switch to ctx.events.append({ type, aggregateId, aggregateType, payload }).
  -->
- 5ee91c6: Jobs see whether they can still defer with `ctx.canDefer`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Jobs see whether they can still defer (ctx.canDefer)
  detail: ctx.canDefer is false when the run is inline or the maxDefers budget is used up, so a handler can write its terminal state instead of deferring into an UnrecoverableError. Behaviour of ctx.defer and the maxDefers failure is unchanged.
  migration: |
    JobContext has a new required field canDefer. Code that builds a JobContext object by hand (boot seeds, test fixtures) adds `canDefer: false` unless the context really supports ctx.defer. Contexts built by the job runner or cast with `as unknown as JobContext` need no change.
  -->
- febcd93: meilisearch is an optional peer dependency
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: meilisearch is an optional peer dependency
  migration: |
    Apps that import @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/search/meilisearch add meilisearch to their own dependencies (bun add meilisearch@^0.58.0); without it that import fails at boot with a message that names the package. Apps without the Meilisearch adapter need nothing.
  -->

- c2fd4b3: preQuery hooks were never invoked by the query pipeline; the hook type, its registry storage and `getPreQueryHooks` are removed.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: preQuery hooks removed
  detail: |
    `r.hook({ type: "preQuery", … })` registered a hook that the query pipeline never called. The `preQuery` hook type, `PreQueryHookFn`, the `preQuery` slot of the hook maps and registrar extension hooks, and `registry.getPreQueryHooks` are removed. A `type: "preQuery"` registration is now a type error and throws at feature registration instead of being silently ignored.
  migration: |
    No known users. Remove `r.hook({ type: "preQuery", … })` registrations; they never ran. To change a query payload, validate or transform it inside the query handler.
  -->
- 8d06990: extraContext factories get the raw db in the test stack and dev, createTenantDb in system mode takes a reason, and a new guard rejects session-level row level security settings.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: testing
  type: breaking
  title: extraContext factories get the raw db in the test stack and dev
  migration: |
    Services built in extraContext that read across tenants at request time, or that a test calls directly, must scope themselves: createTenantDb({ db, tenantId, mode: "system", reason: "<why>" }). Test code reads through stack.db.
  detail: The test stack and dev now pass the enforcing pool to extraContext factories, as runProdApp does, so request-time services keep the ambient request scope and a tenant leak shows up in tests instead of only in production.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: createTenantDb mode system requires a reason
  migration: |
    Add `reason: "<why this access spans tenants>"` to every createTenantDb({ mode: "system" }) call. The reason must be a non-empty string literal: an empty reason throws InternalError at construction, and the internal-subpath-imports guard rejects a missing, empty or non-literal reason.
  detail: The system scope a TenantDb opens for its statements now carries that reason, so a scope leak assertion names the call site. Tenant mode takes no reason.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement
  title: New guard rls-session-settings
  detail: Flags SET and SET SESSION on kumiko.* settings and set_config with is_local false in any source or test string, kumiko.* writes outside rls-scope.ts in non-test code, and a set_config in rls-scope.ts without literal true. A session-level setting survives on a pooled connection and leaks one request's scope into the next.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: testing
  type: improvement
  title: Export applicationRoleUrlOf from kumiko-testing/stack
  detail: Use it to boot runProdApp in tests against the app role. It returns the URL of a database as the non-bypass application role with the password of TEST_DATABASE_URL; pair it with createTestDb({ applicationRole: true }).
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Signature routes read and write secrets in a system scope
  detail: With row level security on, verify() and the handler of a signature route (subscription webhooks, mail connect callbacks) read the secrets of a tenant named by the signed request before any tenant scope exists, and failed. deps.secrets now opens the system scope for each secret access only, so plugin code that parses the unauthenticated body stays unscoped.
  -->
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: testing
  type: improvement
  title: The test application role is realigned to the configured password
  detail: createApplicationRole used to return early when the role existed, so a kumiko_app role with another password made every integration test fail with 28P01. It now runs ALTER ROLE with the configured password and the NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS attributes.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: RLS boot check tells known tables from orphaned ones
  migration: |
    assertRowLevelSecurityBootState takes the known tables as a required third argument: pass knownTablesOf(features), both exported from the db subpath.
  detail: With rowLevelSecurity on, the boot check lists tenant tables without row-level security in two groups. Tables the app schema knows point to kumiko schema generate. Tables no feature declares anymore, including retired framework tables, are named as orphaned and point to dropping them by migration. The check itself stays strict.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement
  title: rls-session-settings also scans .sql files
  detail: Consumer migrations are checked statement by statement for session-level SET kumiko.*, set_config with is_local false and any kumiko.* write.
  -->
- 6d20414: Row level security at runtime: connections set the tenant or system scope in every transaction, one rowLevelSecurity value in kumiko.config.ts drives schema tooling and boot, and the test stack and the dev server run with it on.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Connections set the row level security scope in every transaction
  detail: createDbConnection takes rowLevelSecurity "off" or "on" (default "off", the connection is unchanged). With "on", every statement and transaction sets kumiko.tenant_id and kumiko.scope transaction-locally from the ambient scope. TenantDb sets its tenant, and the system scope for system-mode TenantDbs, global tables and a granted unsafeRaw. Dispatch sets the user's tenant per command, or the system scope for a system-scoped handler. Event store reads and writes use the stream's tenant. Jobs, the event dispatcher, member resolution, migrations, boot seeds, retention, reindex, blind-index cleanup, the PII backfill, projection apply, auth providers and the tenant lifecycle check run in system scope. A statement without a scope sees no tenant rows. The functions that set a scope (runInRowLevelSecurityScope, runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope, tenantRowLevelSecurityScope, systemScopedRunner) are not part of the public db subpath; framework packages import them from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/internal/row-level-security, which no guard closes to apps yet. App code reaches the system scope through a system-scoped handler, a job or a granted unsafeRaw.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: One rowLevelSecurity value in kumiko.config.ts for schema tooling and runners
  detail: AppConfig.rowLevelSecurity ("off" by default) is exported by the managed kumiko/schema.ts as ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY. kumiko-schema generate and validate render and check the policies from it, and apply opens its connection in that mode; the CLI has no flag of its own. The API, worker and all-in-one entrypoints take the same option and refuse a context whose connection runs in another mode. unsafePushTables with "on" reads the catalog first and runs no lock and no DDL for a table that already has ENABLE, FORCE and both kumiko policies.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Projection rebuilds run in system scope under row level security
  detail: The rebuild transaction no longer turns row_security off, so a rebuild works as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS table owner under FORCE. Before the first guard read it locks the live table in SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE mode, which blocks policy DDL and a second rebuild of the same table, and reads the catalog. When row level security is enabled, kumiko_tenant_isolation must exist as a PERMISSIVE policy for ALL commands and PUBLIC and no RESTRICTIVE policy may exist; otherwise the rebuild fails with the table and its policies and leaves the live table untouched. Other permissive policies carry over to the swapped-in table. Multi-stream rebuilds follow the same rule.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: runProdApp checks the row level security state at boot
  detail: RunProdAppOptions.rowLevelSecurity ("off" by default) sets the mode of every connection; the scaffolded server entry passes appConfig.rowLevelSecurity. With "on", boot fails when the database role has SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS, because Postgres then skips every policy, and when a table with tenant_id lacks ENABLE, FORCE or one of the two kumiko policies; the message lists the tables. With "off", boot fails while any table still has row level security enabled and points to the DISABLE migration that kumiko-schema generate writes.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: user-data-rights
  type: fix
  title: User data export and forget cleanup run in system scope
  detail: runUserExport and runForgetCleanup walk every tenant of a user, so they enter the system scope themselves instead of depending on the caller's scope. A direct call outside a job no longer exports or erases nothing under row level security "on".
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: testing
  type: breaking
  title: The test stack runs with row level security on as role kumiko_app
  detail: setupTestStack creates the role kumiko_app (LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, password taken from TEST_DATABASE_URL) once, makes it owner of the test database and opens every pool as that role with rowLevelSecurity "on"; template databases are built the same way. stack.db runs in system scope and sees every tenant's rows as before. The new stack.unscopedDb is the enforced pool the services use, on which a statement without a scope sees no tenant rows. rowLevelSecurity: "off" in the stack options restores the superuser stack without policies. createTestDb takes applicationRole: true for the same setup.
  migration: App code that reads or writes tenant tables through a raw connection outside a request, a job or a TenantDb now sees no rows in integration tests. Test code that calls such a path directly runs it inside runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope or runInRowLevelSecurityScope(tenantRowLevelSecurityScope(tenantId), ...) from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/helpers. Production code works through a TenantDb for the tenant, a job, a system-scoped handler or a granted unsafeRaw. Tests that need superuser rights on stack.db, such as CREATE EXTENSION, CREATE ROLE or event triggers, open their own connection from TEST_DATABASE_URL or use createTestDb(). Manual migration, there is no codemod.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: breaking
  title: The dev server runs with row level security on
  detail: runDevApp and createKumikoServer default to rowLevelSecurity "on" and run the dev stack as kumiko_app. On boot against a persistent dev database, the stack creates the role and transfers ownership of the database and of the public schema's tables, views and sequences to kumiko_app. The database user in DATABASE_URL needs the right to create roles, which the superuser of a local Postgres has. Code that reads tenant tables through a raw connection without a scope sees no rows in development; the boot does not detect this. runSchemaApply takes rowLevelSecurity, and the managed kumiko/schema.ts exports ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY from appConfig; the managed file updates on the next sync.
  migration: Pass rowLevelSecurity: "off" to runDevApp while fixing code paths without tenant context; the dev database keeps kumiko_app as owner. A server entry written by an older scaffold passes appConfig.rowLevelSecurity to runProdApp by hand once the app turns row level security on. Manual migration, there is no codemod.
  -->
- f6d230f: Postgres row level security is on by default, system scopes carry a mandatory reason, and the event write path keeps the caller's tenant scope.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: rowLevelSecurity defaults to "on"
  migration: |
    In the app repo, once with the bump: run `kumiko sync-managed --write` (the managed kumiko/schema.ts now reads `export const ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY = appConfig.rowLevelSecurity;`), then `kumiko schema generate` and commit the migration. It contains ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus the policies `kumiko_tenant_isolation` and `kumiko_system_tenant_read` for every tenant table. The schema apply (the migrate init container in production) creates them; there is no manual database step. Without the migration, boot at "on" refuses to start and names the unprotected tables.
    The app's database role must not skip policies; boot refuses it otherwise. Check it as that role with `SELECT rolsuper, rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user` (both must be false). Callers of createDbConnection without a mode now get "on"; tools that touch no tenant rows (schema baseline/status, the KMS key store) pass "off" explicitly, and the operator commands backfill-pii, waitlist-migrate, project and consumer run on an enforcing connection in system scope, so they work against both modes.
    Way back: set `rowLevelSecurity: "off"` in kumiko.config.ts and run `kumiko schema generate`; the generated migration contains DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and drops the policies. At "off" runProdApp and runWorkerApp log a boot warning.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Boot hooks with a db dependency get a system-scoped db at rowLevelSecurity "on"
  migration: |
    No action unless a hook relied on the unscoped pool. The anonymousAccess factory, enrichAnonymousAccess, the runProdApp `wire` hook and runWorkerApp `wireComponents` now receive a system-scoped db, the same in prod, dev and the test stack, so tenant resolution and boot reads see rows across tenants. Anything the anonymousAccess factory builds keeps that db at request time and therefore reads across tenants for anonymous callers: filter by the resolved tenant yourself. In prod, extraContext factories keep the ambient request scope; the test stack and dev still hand them a system-scoped db, so a service that needs cross-tenant reads at request time must scope itself.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope and systemScopedRunner take a reason
  migration: |
    Call runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope("<why this access spans tenants>", fn) and systemScopedRunner(runner, "<reason>"). An empty or whitespace reason throws InternalError; the scope leak assertion names the reason.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: A projection write under a tenant scope can no longer land in another tenant
  migration: |
    A command that writes an entity row for another tenant through ctx.db now fails with SQLSTATE 42501; move that write to ctx.systemDb.acknowledgeCrossTenant in an r.systemScope() feature.
  detail: applyEntityEvent keeps an ambient tenant scope instead of wrapping every write in a system scope. Writes for other tenants go through ctx.systemDb.acknowledgeCrossTenant in an r.systemScope() feature. Replays, rebuilds and global entities still write system scoped.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement
  title: New guard internal-subpath-imports
  detail: Flags kumiko-framework/internal/* imports outside the framework repo, row level security scope helpers from kumiko-testing/helpers in non-test code, and system scope calls without a literal reason.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: jobs
  type: fix
  title: Tenant job run rows are written in the tenant's scope
  detail: With row level security on, the queued, started and finished rows of tenant-visible job runs were rejected by Postgres when the job was dispatched outside a request scope, and the logger only logged the error. The logger now scopes its tenant writes to the job's tenant and logs a rejected write as a missing row-level-security scope instead of a generic write failure.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: composeFeatures no longer warns about its own bundled copies
  detail: Composing the output of a first composeFeatures pass again drops the earlier bundled instances silently; only copies the app supplied itself still warn.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Scoped pool statements pipeline their transaction
  detail: A pool statement under a row level security scope sends BEGIN, the transaction-local scope, the statement and COMMIT pipelined on one reserved connection instead of waiting for each, which cuts its roundtrips roughly in half. The connection returns to the pool only after COMMIT settled.
  -->
- 22f9f23: The tenant aggregate is now a global systemStream entity: its stream, read row and search bucket live on SYSTEM_TENANT_ID.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant
  type: breaking
  title: Tenant streams and rows live on the system tenant, seed defaults changed
  detail: Tenants created, renamed or toggled by a SystemAdmin whose session tenant was neither 0001 nor the SYSTEM tenant landed in the event stream, read row and search bucket of that session tenant, so later updates could not find them. The tenant entity is now declared systemStream with tenancy global, so every writer (create, update, enable and disable, request and cancel destruction, the destroy job stages) addresses the stream on SYSTEM_TENANT_ID. seedTenant, seedUser, seedAdmin and seedAdminGuarded default to createSystemUser(SYSTEM_TENANT_ID) and write the tenant to SYSTEM whatever tenant an explicit by acts from; managed-pages and compliance-profiles seeds default to createSystemUser(tenantId). Existing memberships written by an admin of another tenant sit on that admin's stream while read_tenant_memberships.tenant_id carries the member tenant; after the backfill streamTenantId equals tenantId for them. New export backfillTenantStreamTenants from the tenant feature, the boot step runStreamTenantBackfillOnBoot in server-runtime, EsOperationType gains "stream-migration", built on the generic backfillAggregateStreamTenants in shared (backfillUserStreamTenants keeps its signature).
  migration: |
    Nothing to run: runProdApp (api, all-in-one) and runWorkerApp search for legacy tenant, membership and user streams on every boot, before the boot seeds respectively before the worker starts, and fix what they find. A boot with nothing left reads only events of other tenants than SYSTEM (plus the membership events) and does no rebuild or reindex. It merges split tenant streams onto SYSTEM_TENANT_ID, moves each membership stream to the tenantId of its payload, moves legacy user streams, removes stale search documents from the old buckets, and where streams moved rebuilds tenant:projection:tenant-entity, tenant:projection:tenant-membership-entity and user:projection:user-entity and reindexes the tenant and user search indexes. Legacy streams written by old pods during a rolling deploy are fixed on the next boot. A row in kumiko_es_operations (stream-tenant-backfill:<user|tenant>:derived-pending) marks a run in progress so that a crash after the moves still gets its rebuild and reindex. Parallel boots are serialized by a Postgres advisory lock; failures are logged (aggregateId, step, error) and retried on the next boot. A process without a search adapter leaves the work to one that has it. Library users can call backfillTenantStreamTenants or backfillUserStreamTenantsWithDerivedState directly. Code that read tenant streams with loadAggregate(db, tenantId, "tenant") or appended tenant events with the tenant id as stream tenant must use SYSTEM_TENANT_ID. Consumer workarounds that wrote tenant streams under a SystemAdmin `by` (for example an executor update with TestUsers.systemAdmin) are no longer needed, because the stream is always SYSTEM. Seeds that relied on the old by default (TestUsers.systemAdmin) now get the system user as audit actor. Apps without a search backend set `search: "none"` on runProdApp and runWorkerApp, otherwise the stream-tenant backfill stays deferred in every process that has no search adapter.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 1a7eebe: Parallel writes on one handler transaction no longer abort it, a failed verb leaves no orphan event, invalid date values are a 400, and previewOpenByDefault opens the newest file.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Parallel writes in one handler no longer abort the transaction
  detail: Bun.SQL does not serialize savepoints on a transaction. A handler that started several executor writes on ctx.db with Promise.all opened overlapping savepoints, the first RELEASE also released its neighbours, and the next one aborted the whole transaction with a 500. runInSavepoint and runInSavepointIfSupported now queue savepoints per transaction (proxy runners over the same transaction share one queue, savepoints opened from inside a running one still nest), and an executor verb on a handler transaction now runs in its own savepoint: when it fails, its event append, projection and hooks roll back together, also when the handler catches the failure, so no event without projection is left behind and a rebuild replays cleanly. Postgres errors 22007 and 22008 (a date or time value the column rejects, such as 2026-02-30) now map to a 400 validation_error instead of a 500, on writes and on query filters.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer
  type: fix
  title: previewOpenByDefault opens the newest file
  detail: FileValueList with previewOpenByDefault (renderer format "file") now opens only the PDF preview of the newest file instead of the first one. Uploads append their FileRef id, so the newest file is the last id in fileIds.
  -->
- 21b70ba: New guard that fails when a consumer passes anything but FEATURES from kumiko/schema to runSchemaCli.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement

  detail: The replay behind kumiko-schema validate tracks ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and policy definitions per table, follows table renames, and reports row-level-security-drift when the committed SQL does not produce the policies the snapshot expects (missing, extra, altered or hand-edited) or turns on row level security for a table the snapshot has no spec for. - 1b3a297: Bun.SQL is the only Postgres driver and the postgres-js fork is gone.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Bun.SQL replaces postgres-js as the only Postgres driver
  detail: createDbConnection opens a Bun.SQL pool and needs Bun 1.4.4 or newer, the first release that drops a cached statement plan after DDL on the same connection. The handle gains listenClient for LISTEN/NOTIFY. Server errors carry the code ERR_POSTGRES_SERVER_ERROR with the SQLSTATE in errno and the constraint name in constraint; connection failures carry ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED, ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_REFUSED, ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT or ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_FAILED. extractPgError, isUniqueViolation, isTableAlreadyExists, constraintOf and the newly exported isUndefinedTable read that shape. The onNotice option is removed, because Bun.SQL has no notice hook and drops server notices. The ssl option takes Bun's tls value (a boolean, "disable", "prefer", "require", "verify-ca", "verify-full" or a TLS options object); ssl true and a TLS object without rejectUnauthorized still verify the server certificate, as they did with postgres-js. DB_PROVIDER is refused at boot for every non-empty value, "postgres" included.
  migration: Read SQLSTATE and constraint only through extractPgError or the is* helpers from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db; a direct err.code === "23505" check or an err.constraint_name read no longer matches. Replace checks for CONNECTION_CLOSED, CONNECTION_ENDED, CONNECTION_DESTROYED or CONNECT_TIMEOUT with the ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_* codes. Drop onNotice from createDbConnection calls. Remove DB_PROVIDER from every environment. Run on Bun 1.4.4 or newer in engines, CI and images. Code that imports postgres itself must declare its own dependency or move to Bun.SQL, since the framework no longer installs it. Manual migration, there is no codemod.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: types
  type: breaking
  title: DbConnection, DbTx and PgClient are Bun.SQL types and postgres is no longer a peer dependency
  detail: DbConnection is SQL | RawDbClient, DbTx is TransactionSQL | RawDbClient and PgClient is SQL from the bun module, so the package type-checks against bun-types instead of postgres. The postgres peer dependency is removed.
  migration: Remove postgres from your dependencies unless your own code imports it. Annotations that named postgres.Sql or postgres.TransactionSql for framework handles become SQL and TransactionSQL from "bun", or the DbConnection and DbTx aliases. Manual migration, there is no codemod.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: testing

  migration: Tests that compared the captured error's code with CONNECTION_CLOSED compare with ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED or call isClosedConnectionError. Manual migration, there is no codemod.
  -->

On Bun 1.4.4 the resolver auto-installs tailwindcss next to a renderer copy in Bun's install cache, so a build without a node_modules tree took the fallback and then failed in Tailwind with "Can't resolve 'tailwindcss'".   detail: The selector field id of a provider form is qualified with its owner feature, so the translation keys of its option labels change.
  migration: move app translation overrides from config:entity:__config-edit__:field:provider:option:<value> to the owner-qualified field id, field:mail-foundation-provider:option:<value> or field:file-foundation-provider:option:<value>
  -->
- 2602c62: Signature extra routes get `deps.dispatchWriteAs({ handlerQn, payload, tenantId, roles })`, a write as the tenant's system user with the "system" role plus exactly the named roles, without SystemAdmin. E2E extra seeders get `ctx.writeAs(roles, handlerQn, payload)` bound to the seeded tenant, so a seeder can write to handlers gated on app roles without adding the role "system" to production handlers.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: E2E seeders and signature routes can write with explicit roles
  detail: dispatchWriteAs on signature route deps and writeAs on the E2E seeder context run a write as the tenant's system user with the "system" role plus the given roles, without SystemAdmin. write() keeps running as SystemAdmin.
  -->
- 8449190: Handlers get `ctx.scheduleAfterRollback(fn)`, the counterpart of `scheduleAfterCommit` for compensating work outside the transaction.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: ctx.scheduleAfterRollback for outside-transaction compensation
  detail: ctx.scheduleAfterRollback(fn) runs fn when the handler transaction does not commit, or when the enclosing savepoint of a nested ctx.write rolls back (after the outer transaction ends). It never runs on commit, errors are logged and do not change the write result, and it is absent outside a transaction scope (perCommand, post-commit, beforeTransaction, member resolution). A failed COMMIT also triggers it, so callbacks must be idempotent and outcome-safe, for example releasing a reservation row that may already be gone.
  -->
- 080c5e7: Mails sent outside a handler as the system tenant can read their attachments: `SystemWireDeps` carries `filesForTenant`, and `buildSystemChannelContext` builds a channel context with `readAttachment` set.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: buildSystemChannelContext for system tenant mails outside a handler
  detail: buildSystemChannelContext(deps, { config, secrets }) returns a ChannelContext for the system tenant whose readAttachment reads file and inline attachments. SystemWireDeps (wire hook and runWorkerApp wireComponents) has a new required filesForTenant that deps can pass straight in.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: filesForTenant in SystemWireDeps
  detail: The wire hook and the worker wireComponents receive filesForTenant, built from the AppContext after buildServer wired it. ApiEntrypoint and WorkerEntrypoint expose that context as entrypoint.context.
  -->
- 76c95ae: TenantDb gets `upsert(table, values, { conflictTarget, update? })`, a tenant-safe INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Tenant-safe upsert on ctx.db
  detail: ctx.db.upsert(table, values, { conflictTarget, update? }) requires tenantId in conflictTarget and the target to match a declared unique index or primary key. The update only touches the row of the inserted tenant, update may not set tenantId, and the default update leaves conflict, primary-key and tenant columns alone. Event-fed tables are rejected. Replaces unsafeRaw plus upsertOnConflict for tenant-scoped upserts.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- ed98312: Settle and consume racing on a swept cap reservation book their units again, schema status and baseline use one connection, package lookups no longer auto-install from the registry, and fresh scaffolds build with `bun run build`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-counter
  type: fix
  title: Settle and consume racing on a swept reservation book their units
  detail: After the sweep deleted a reservation's row, a consume could commit its released tombstone between the two reads of a parallel settle or consume. That call took the released tombstone for a settled one, so settle reported success without booking its amount and a second consume was rejected with cap_reservation_settled. Only a settled tombstone counts as settled now; a released one runs into the insert conflict and the retry books against it.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: schema status and baseline use one connection, bun-types is a peer dependency
  detail: kumiko schema status and baseline open a pool of one connection instead of the default size, because Bun.SQL dials every pool connection on the first query. bun-types is now a peer dependency (^1.4.4) of framework, types, server-runtime and dev-server instead of a regular dependency, so install it next to the framework.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: Package lookups no longer auto-install from the registry
  detail: The new @cosmicdrift/kumiko-server-runtime/resolve-installed-package export looks up node_modules before asking Bun.resolveSync, which installs missing packages from the registry since Bun 1.4.4. The prod build, the dev-server stylesheet lookup and the handbuch commands use it.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: improvement
  title: Scaffolded docker-compose raises Postgres max_connections to 300
  detail: Bun.SQL dials its whole pool eagerly, so the default limit of 100 is too tight for an app plus its tests. Existing apps can add command postgres -c max_connections=300 to the postgres service.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: fix
  title: Fresh scaffolds build with bun run build
  detail: create-kumiko-app now writes public/index.html with the /styles.css and /client.js placeholders. Without it kumiko-build stopped with a missing-template error, so the scaffolded Dockerfile could not build either.
  -->
- 641f268: `maxPerTenant` counts active and waiting jobs in one snapshot per queue.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: maxPerTenant counts active and waiting jobs in one snapshot
  detail: The guard read the active and the waiting list with separate Redis calls, so a job that moved from waiting to active between them was missing from both and a dispatch over the cap got through. It now reads both lists with one getJobs snapshot per queue. The integration tests hold the cap jobs on a release gate instead of sleeping.
  -->
- dd5fd28: The access-invalidation consumer no longer ends up dead-lettered during a longer Redis outage. It keeps retrying with an exponential backoff (250 ms up to 10 s) until the publish goes through, so later revocations still reach open SSE streams once Redis is back. Only failed publishes are exempt from the attempt limit; any other failure (a poison event) still dead-letters at the dispatcher limit. `EventConsumerErrorPolicy` gains `isTransientError` for consumers that need the same split.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Access invalidation survives a Redis outage
  detail: The consumer that pushes session, token and membership revocations to open streams does not count failed publishes towards the attempt limit and backs off between them, instead of dying after 10 failed deliveries and silently dropping later revocations. Other failures keep the limit. New EventConsumerErrorPolicy.isTransientError.
  -->
- a50674e: An upload that names a record re-checks the record lock in the transaction that inserts the file row. Before, the lock was only checked before the bytes were read and stored, so a record locked in between still received the file; the upload now answers 409 `record_locked` and removes the bytes.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: file upload rechecks the record lock when inserting the row
  detail: POST /files with an entityId reads the stored row again through the inserting transaction and refuses with 409 record_locked when lockedWhen holds. The window between that read and the commit stays open, like for any other write that checks the lock before its own commit.
  -->
- 53e2a0e: Documents the limit of the Meilisearch default-config upgrade: after a restart, an index whose stored settings are a strict subset of the current registry default is treated as an older default and widened again.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Meilisearch default upgrade cannot tell a narrowed configure() from an older default
  detail: A tenant that called configure() with a strict subset of the default attributes gets the full default back after the next process restart, because Meilisearch stores no marker for an explicit configure(). Configure the full attribute set, or a set that contains an attribute outside the default, to keep it.
  -->
- ab1ca17: The per-process audit dedup of system cron escape hatches keys a target only for `global-write`, where it names a table. A `cross-tenant-read` cron no longer adds a dedup entry and an audit event per touched foreign row; it audits once per day and process. Entries older than the re-audit interval were already swept.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Cross-tenant-read crons audit once per day, not once per foreign row
  detail: The process dedup key of a declared system cron hatch includes the target only for global-write (a table). Row targets of cross-tenant-read no longer grow the in-memory map or write one audit event per row.
  -->
- 5b72552: A boot gate that runs into its timeout now settles (bounded) before `start()` rejects, so the abandoned gate handler cannot keep writing to the database and Redis while the process shuts down, even if the caller never invokes `stop()`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Failed job-runner start waits for the timed-out boot gate
  detail: start() now waits a bounded time for an abandoned boot gate before throwing, instead of leaving that to stop(). The scheduler-seen timer is only started after every step that can fail, so no timer outlives a failed start.
  -->
- 768a67e: Switching off a toggleable feature no longer hides the workspace of an active feature that declares the same short workspace id. The tenant-level strip now compares the owning feature of each workspace instead of only its short id.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: disabled feature no longer removes another feature's workspace with the same id
  detail: buildAppSchema records which feature owns each workspace and the feature strip removes only the workspaces of the disabled features. Two features that use the same short workspace id keep their own entries.
  -->
- d8f9c73: The upload ledger stamps rows with the injected `AppContext.clock` (the source behind `ctx.tz`) instead of the wall clock, so the orphan-upload sweep and the ledger agree under a controlled clock. The test stack passes its `extraContext.clock` through.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: upload ledger uses the injected clock
  detail: createFileUploadLedger and withUploadLedger take an optional now function, and the file provider resolver wires AppContext.clock into it. Without a clock the system time is used as before.
  -->
- 91fb415: Anonymous saves never bind a pending upload. All anonymous visitors share one user id, so the pending-upload check refuses them in the shared predicate used by `bindPendingFileRef`, `loadPendingFileRef` and the save pipeline. A test now saves as one visitor with the file id another visitor stored and checks it stays unbound.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: anonymous save leaves foreign pending uploads unbound
  detail: Integration test through the real write route with anonymous access, covering the save pipeline path of the pending-upload ownership check.
  -->
- a50674e: Live signals no longer name row ids to roles that only read some rows. When an entity's own `access.read` is an ownership map (for example `Driver: from("user:id", "assigneeId")`), a connection whose roles do not include an `"all"` rule gets the entity signal without `id` and `version`, like a row-filtered query result.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: live signals hide row ids from row-filtered roles
  detail: createSseRoute takes an optional entityRowReadMaps option, built from entity access.read by the server routes. A signed-in connection receives id and version only if the entity has no read ownership map or one of its roles is mapped to all; otherwise the signal carries just the entity and event type so the client refetches.
  -->
- 5b707a6: The echoed write event is now removed from the response at the dispatcher boundary instead of being hidden on the result object. A handler that copies the executor result with a spread (`{ ...created.data, extra }`) keeps the event, so projections and postSave hooks fire again for it.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: write handlers that spread the executor result keep projections and postSave hooks
  detail: The event is stripped from lifecycle results when the dispatcher masks the response, no longer made non-enumerable on the result, so copying the result does not lose it. Responses still carry no event.
  -->
- cee9e32: Tests now prove that the echoed write event is absent from `dispatcher.write` and `dispatcher.batch` results and from agent tool call results, the entry points used by websocket writes, agent tools and jobs.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: event-free write results proven for non-HTTP entry points
  detail: Integration tests assert that dispatcher.write, dispatcher.batch and the agent tool dispatch return no event. No runtime change: all of them already pass through the dispatcher masking.
  -->
- aa83c70: `seedReferenceData` now adopts reference-data rows that were seeded before the event-store executor existed. Such rows have no events, so changing a value after the upgrade failed the boot with a stream-version conflict and a projection rebuild dropped the rows. The seeder now deletes the eventless row and re-creates it under the same id through the executor.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: reference-data seed adopts rows that have no event stream
  detail: Rows from installs that seeded reference data by direct insert are re-created under the same id through the executor on the next boot, so updates apply and the rows survive a rebuild. No action is needed; the row id is unchanged, only its version restarts at 1.
  -->
- a50674e: `POST /api/client-errors` keeps a per-process rate limit when the shared limiter is configured. Before, a Redis outage made the fail-open shared limiter the only protection and an anonymous caller could flood the log pipeline; now the in-memory window of 10 reports per minute per IP always applies as a floor.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: client-errors route keeps an in-memory floor limit
  detail: The in-memory per-IP limiter now runs in front of the Redis-backed limiter instead of only when no resolver is wired, so a failing resolver can no longer lift the limit on the public client-errors endpoint.
  -->
- 80399a2: `reindexEntity` now lifts the server `statement_timeout` for each batch scan with `SET LOCAL` in a short transaction on the runner it was given. Before, it asked `withoutStatementTimeout` for an unbounded pool, which silently passed through for the gated runner that `ctx.systemDb.unsafeRaw()` returns, so the reindex job still ran under the 60 s cap.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: reindex job batches are no longer cut off by the server statement timeout
  detail: reindexEntity reads each batch in its own transaction with statement_timeout lifted for that transaction, on the caller's own runner, so the job path through ctx.systemDb.unsafeRaw() keeps its gates.
  -->
- a50674e: `GET /files/meta?ids=` is charged by the number of ids when a rate-limit resolver is wired. Each id costs a KMS-decrypting read, so one request for 100 ids now takes 100 from a per-user budget of 1000 ids per minute instead of counting as a single request.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: files meta batch route is rate limited by id count
  detail: createFileRoutes takes an optional metaBatchRateLimitResolver, wired by the server from the rate-limit resolver or Redis. A user over 1000 requested ids per minute gets 429 rate_limited; a failing limiter fails open and is reported like the other limiters.
  -->
- ff84ee4: `kumiko-upgrade` without `--apply` now says that the upgrade CHANGELOG and the marker are only written by `--apply`, whenever changes are pending or the marker is behind the installed version.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: kumiko-upgrade explains that --apply writes the CHANGELOG
  detail: The preview run never wrote the upgrade CHANGELOG or the marker, and consumers running it without --apply got no entry and no explanation. It now prints a hint; the exit code is unchanged.
  -->
- 2602c62: Codemods that add an import now place it after the last existing import instead of inside a file's header comment block.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Codemod imports no longer land inside header comments
  detail: ensureNamedImport appends the new import after the last existing import, so a file with a header comment block keeps the comment intact.
  -->
- 2602c62: `readDatabaseNow` returns the database clock at millisecond precision, matching `events.created_at`, so comparing it against stored timestamps no longer tips on microseconds.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Database now is rounded to milliseconds
  detail: The Postgres clock read behind readDatabaseNow is cast to timestamptz(3), the precision of events.created_at, so a comparison with a stored event time is exact.
  -->
- 2602c62: List filters on a `reference` field with `multiple: true` use jsonb containment like `multiSelect`, so eq, ne and in match rows whose id array contains the value.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: List filter on multiple references matches array contents
  detail: eq, ne and in on a multi-reference field now check jsonb containment instead of scalar equality, and screen filters on such fields allow the equality operators. Consumers no longer need a full scan.
  -->
- 2602c62: `kumiko-upgrade --resolve` now also sets the resolved manual migrations to `[migrated]` or `[not-applicable]` in the app's CHANGELOG.md, not only in the marker.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: kumiko-upgrade --resolve updates CHANGELOG.md
  detail: The Manual migrations lines of every CHANGELOG.md section change from [open] to the chosen resolution for the resolved ids; other entries and files without a CHANGELOG.md are left alone.
  -->
