## 0.388.0

### Minor Changes

- e1c01e4: The entity list query takes an optional `aggregate` payload and answers with groups and measures instead of rows, so a table can show group headers and sums over all matching rows rather than one page.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Groups and sums on the entity list query
  detail: Pass aggregate with an optional groupBy field and up to 20 measures (sum, avg, count, min, max per field) to a list query. The answer is groups with key, count, one value per measure in request order and, for a reference groupBy, the label of the referenced row. Screen filters, search, ownership and field read access apply exactly as for rows; a field the caller may not read yields null or no groups, and encrypted, personal or secret fields and unsuitable field types are rejected with a validation error. At most 200 groups are returned, with truncated set beyond that. Custom query handlers use executor.aggregate or answerListAggregate.
  -->
- ee0aaf9: Write handlers can book rateLimit tokens per payload element with `rateLimitCost`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: rateLimitCost for write handlers
  detail: A write handler can declare `rateLimitCost: (payload) => number`. The result is booked on every declared `rateLimit` bucket instead of the options' static `cost`; values below 1 count as 1 and non-finite values fail the request. The bucket is charged after schema validation, so an invalid payload costs nothing, and a rejected request consumes no tokens. Boot fails when `rateLimitCost` is set without an active `rateLimit`, or on an anonymous or ip-limited handler, because the cost books after the parse and such a handler would lose its pre-parse protection.
  migration: Optional. Bulk handlers should add `rateLimitCost: (p) => p.files.length` so a request with many items is not counted as one.
  -->
- 22bc0a7: Review fixes: seeded layout titles resolve in the PDF editor and mail rail, the client-error rate limiter evicts the least recently seen IPs instead of resetting every window, the SSE heartbeat ping counts towards stalled-client detection, and the `__Host-` session cookies are expired even with `secureCookies:false`. The exported `runAsDirectCallEntry` is now `runAsAgentToolCallEntry`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: document-designer
  type: fix
  title: Seeded layout titles show translated in the PDF editor and mail rail
  detail: A layout seeded with a title i18n key now shows its translated name in the PDF editor header and the mail editor properties rail instead of the raw key.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Client-error rate limit survives address rotation
  detail: Without Redis, the per-process limiter now drops the least recently seen IPs when more than 10000 are tracked, so a flood of fresh addresses no longer resets the window of every other IP.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Stalled SSE clients are dropped without further broadcasts
  detail: The heartbeat ping is written and tracked like entity frames instead of awaited, so a client that stopped reading is aborted at the next heartbeat after the stall timeout and releases its broker slot.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Leftover __Host- cookies are expired with secureCookies:false too
  detail: Clearing the session cookies now always sends the Secure delete for the __Host- auth and csrf variants when the configured names are unprefixed, so an app switched to secureCookies:false behind a TLS proxy no longer keeps a stale __Host- csrf cookie.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: runAsDirectCallEntry renamed to runAsAgentToolCallEntry
  detail: The internal request-context helper also marks its scope as an agent tool call, so the name now says so; it stays reserved for dispatchToolCall.
  migration: replace imports of runAsDirectCallEntry from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/internal/request-context with runAsAgentToolCallEntry; the signature is unchanged
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 7e54012: `runProdApp` passes `errorDocs` and `instanceId` to the server. `ApiEntrypointOptions` now carries both fields. Before, the entrypoint dropped them silently, so the `errorDocs` option of `runProdApp` had no effect, and a `KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID` set only in a custom `envSource` never reached the server, which fell back to `process.env`. The boot-abort cleanup of `runProdApp` moved into a helper that also swallows synchronously throwing cleanups, and `wireDevAuth` now takes only the config fields it reads.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: runProdApp passes errorDocs and instanceId to the server
  detail: ApiEntrypointOptions now carries errorDocs and instanceId and createApiEntrypoint forwards them to the server. Before, runProdApp dropped its errorDocs option, and a KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID set only in a custom envSource never reached the server, which fell back to process.env. The boot-abort cleanup of runProdApp also moved into a helper that swallows synchronously throwing cleanups.
  -->
- f81f639: The registry checks physical-table collisions against the table name the DDL creates, so two entities of different features with the same physical table now fail at boot. `WorkerEntrypointOptions` carries `instanceId`, and `runWorkerApp` reads `KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID` from its `envSource`. The PII and retention validator, the cascade-delete hook, `computeListViewModel`, `applyFormatSpec` and the field projection of `buildAppSchema` are rule tables with unchanged messages and order, and the remaining German dev messages are English.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Physical-table collisions use the DDL table name
  detail: createRegistry compared entity tables under a feature-prefixed name that no DDL path creates, so an entity whose explicit table equals another feature's derived table name, or two entities with the same explicit table in different features, registered fine and then emitted the same CREATE TABLE twice. The check now uses the unprefixed physical name, the same as the store-table check and the migrate runner.
  migration: Apps where two entities share a physical table name fail at boot with "has physical table ... which collides with entity ...". Give one of them a different `table`.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Worker entrypoint takes instanceId
  detail: WorkerEntrypointOptions now carries instanceId (moved to BaseEntrypointOptions, so the API and all-in-one options keep it) and createWorkerEntrypoint forwards it to the server. runWorkerApp reads KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID from its envSource like runProdApp, so with KUMIKO_INSTANCE_ID set, per-instance consumers in the worker and its app.started event use the same id. Before, the worker server only saw process.env.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: PII, retention and cascade-delete rules as tables, English dev messages
  detail: validatePiiAndRetention runs one checker per rule in a fixed order, and the cascade-delete hook dispatches each relation through a table of onDelete strategies. Error and warning texts, their order, transaction boundaries and event order are unchanged. buildAppSchema forwards field properties through an ordered table, and kumiko-upgrade and the pii-personal-migration codemod run one function per step; their output is byte-identical. The dev warnings of normalizeListColumn and buildAppSchema are now English.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer
  type: improvement
  title: List view model and cell formats as tables
  detail: computeListViewModel resolves each column through an ordered list of resolvers and applyFormatSpec dispatches through a table of cell formatters. Output is unchanged; a format named like an Object.prototype member such as "toString" still takes the unknown-format path.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: improvement
  title: English buildServerBundle errors
  detail: The errors for a missing bin/main.ts and a missing bin/kumiko.ts in buildServerBundle are now English.
  -->
- bd38fdc: The list read verb, the column builder for entity fields, the derivation of entity table metadata and the per-table migration diff are split into small named steps. Generated SQL, list results, table metadata and migration plans are unchanged.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Named steps for list reads, field columns, table metadata and table diffs
  detail: The list read verb runs search, sort, cursor boundary, filters, stream-version projection, row rehydration and the next cursor as named steps in their own files next to event-store-executor-read.ts, and detail() shares the ownership and row rehydration steps. Field columns come from one emitter per field type in a typed table, so a new field type fails the typecheck until it has an emitter, and an unknown type from untyped input still throws "unhandled field type". deriveEntityTableMeta collects columns, foreign-key, blind-index and declared indexes in separate steps with the same overloads and error texts. diffOneTable compares columns and indexes through one comparator per kind and keeps the order of added, dropped and changed entries.
  -->
- 7447ac1: The feature AST matches pattern ids, classifies editability and renders patterns through one typed table per kind instead of long switch statements. Rendered source, editability and id matching are unchanged.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Per-kind tables for feature-AST id matching, editability and rendering
  detail: callMatchesId() looks up one matcher per PatternId kind in a typed table in feature-ast/pattern-id-matchers.ts next to patch.ts. getEditability() reads a table keyed by pattern kind, and renderPattern() dispatches through one renderer per pattern kind. All three tables are typed over their kind union, so a new kind does not compile until it has an entry. The feature-ast barrel exports the same names as before.
  -->
- 7e54012: `validateBoot` now calls `validateProjectionAllowlist`. Violations that passed silently before fail at boot: `unsafeProjectionUpsert`/`unsafeProjectionDelete` without `r.requires.projection`, on aggregate tables, tier-2 steps without `r.requires.step`, pipeline closures that read the payload while the step list is built, and two features registering the same aggregate table. Aggregate tables are matched by their physical table name, so an entity without an explicit `table` is protected as well.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Boot enforces the projection allowlist
  detail: The projection allowlist validator existed but was never called from validateBoot. It now runs as the last cross-feature check. It also keys aggregate tables by the physical table name (entity.table or the derived read_* name) instead of the entity name, so unsafeProjection steps on the table of an entity without an explicit table, and duplicate tables between a derived and an explicit name, are detected.

  -->

  detail: handleJob() claimed the sequential lock before prepareJobRun() and the onJobStart hook, but only released it in the finally block that started after them. A throwing onJobStart left the lock until its TTL (305 s) and every further invocation of that job was requeued behind it. Both calls now run inside the try and the lock is released by job name. - ff5f68e: The boot seed dispatcher of `runProdApp` now runs the same write lifecycle as the dispatcher behind `/api/*`. Before, it got no lifecycle hooks, so seed writes and seed migrations (`seedsDir`) skipped the whole lifecycle: a file a seed stored with `createFileRef` and `attachTo` was never bound to the record the seed wrote (it kept `entity_id = null` and the file access guard answered 404 for everyone but the uploader), and preSave, postSave, preDelete and postDelete hooks, the tenant check of file references and the disposal of removed file references did not run either.
  
  What changes for existing apps: seeds now go through the same hooks as a user write. A hook that throws inside the transaction fails the seed and with it the boot. Seeds that write on every boot run their hooks on every update, because the dedup key includes the handler version. File binding applies to seeds that write as the system user, which is the user `createFileRef` uploads as.
  
  `ApiEntrypoint`, `AllInOneEntrypoint` and `KumikoServer` expose the hooks as `lifecycleHooks`, the same instance the API dispatcher uses.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Seed writes run the save lifecycle, so seeded files bind to their records
  detail: runProdApp built the boot seed dispatcher without lifecycle hooks, so seed writes and seed migrations skipped file binding (entity_id stayed null, other users got 404), the pre/post save and delete hooks, the tenant check of file references and the disposal of removed file references. The seed dispatcher now reuses the lifecycle hooks of the API dispatcher, exposed as lifecycleHooks on the entrypoints and on KumikoServer. A hook that throws inside the transaction now fails the seed and the boot.
  -->

## 0.383.1

### Patch Changes

- 4ea38e1: Closing a database connection now also closes the unbounded pools that `withoutStatementTimeout` opened for runs that never finished, so a reindex abandoned by a caller-side timeout no longer keeps the database open after shutdown.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: close() ends unbounded pools of abandoned long runs
  detail: withoutStatementTimeout (reindexEntity, PII backfill, projection and multi-stream rebuilds, event-store index builds) runs on its own pool without statement_timeout and closes it when the run settles. A run that never settles, such as a reindex a boot rebuild gave up on via its own timeout, kept that pool connected, so DROP DATABASE in test cleanup failed with "is being accessed by other users". The connection handle's close() now ends these pools too. A rebuild that is still running when close() is called is ended after the same close timeout instead of keeping shutdown waiting.
  -->
- @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types@0.383.1

- 9ef4b39: Database load and pagination hardening plus a job-defer API: server-side statement (60 s) and idle-in-transaction (300 s) timeouts, concurrent session lookups, page-only tenant decryption, keyset scans in reindex, purge and escape-hatch retention, and `ctx.defer(ms)` for jobs.

Opt out per limit by setting the variable to 0, or change it, with DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS, DATABASE_IDLE_IN_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS and DATABASE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS (for example DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS=0); createDbConnection takes statementTimeoutMs, idleInTransactionSessionTimeoutMs and lockTimeoutMs. Migrations, projection and multi-stream rebuilds, search reindex, PII backfills and the CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY helpers run without the statement cap (withoutStatementTimeout). A custom long-running statement on the app pool now needs the same helper or a higher limit.
  -->

  title: sessionChecker looks up the user and the membership concurrently
  detail: The session check starts the user lookup together with the session read and the membership lookup together with the last-seen refresh. Results and the fail-open behavior are unchanged; a failed lookup that is not needed no longer raises an unhandled rejection.

- 07ccdc9: The compile-time write lock on event-fed tables is fail-closed: a write compiles only for a Writable table or a runner that carries the executor capability, so type-erased tables are rejected instead of accepted.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Writes compile only for Writable tables or capable runners
  detail: The negative ExecutorOnly brand is replaced by positive brands. table(), defineUnmanagedTable and deriveEntityTableMeta with source "unmanaged" return Writable tables; buildEntityTable and r.projection tables do not. insertOne, updateMany, deleteMany, the upsert and counter helpers and the TenantDb and db.global() write methods accept a Writable table, or any table when the runner is an ExecutorManagedRunner or ExecutorManagedTenantDb. Widening a table to SchemaTable or EntityTableMeta drops the brand, so erased tables no longer compile. Projection apply functions receive tx as ExecutorManagedRunner. The runtime lock is unchanged.
  migration: Apply functions that annotate `tx` as `DbRunner`, inline or standalone, type it as `ExecutorManagedRunner` (or drop the annotation / annotate the function with SingleStreamApplyFn/MultiStreamApplyFn). Own write helpers take `WritableTable` for direct-write tables, or `ExecutorManagedRunner` / `ExecutorManagedTenantDb` when they write event-fed tables from an apply, rebuild or tenant-destroy context, instead of `SchemaTable`/`EntityTableMeta`. Tables annotated as `SchemaTable` lose the `Writable` brand; drop the annotation or add `& Writable`. Tenant-destroy hooks keep using the db they receive. Affects kumiko-enterprise, solon, money-horse, kumiko-studio, publicstatus.
  -->

The executor, projection apply, rebuild, unsafeProjectionDelete, tenant-destroy hooks and deleteRowsWithoutReplayableStream hold it; ctx.db.unsafeRaw() never does. Retention deletes only rows whose stream is gone or archived. The cascade delete hook, the soft-delete purge jobs and seedReferenceData now write through the executor, so their effect survives a rebuild; cascade children are written as the system user, and softDelete children are soft-deleted instead of hard-deleted. The direct-entity-writes guard has no exceptions left.

Test seeds and teardown use seedRow, seedRows, updateRows, deleteRows and clearTables from kumiko-testing instead of hand-written wipe helpers. Do not pass ctx.db.unsafeRaw() to code that deletes event-fed rows; pass ctx.db inside a tenant-destroy hook. Retention code calls deleteRowsWithoutReplayableStream after pruning or archiving the events. seedReferenceData takes the registry instead of a table map. Affects kumiko-enterprise, kumiko-studio and solon.

## 0.378.0

### Minor Changes

- 2d7ee3e: Document PDFs can embed the images of a record
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: improvement
  title: Document PDFs embed the images of a record
  detail: A template variable of type images (templateVariable.images()) holds FileRef ids of the record. The new Images block (div[data-images], PDF templates only, rejected for mail kinds) renders them as data-URI images in the real PDF render. Only files of the rendering tenant are read, only png, jpeg, gif and webp, at most 24 images and 20 MB per document; missing, foreign, oversized or non-image ids are dropped silently. Previews and draft PDFs never read files and show one placeholder box per block. An images variable never renders as inline text. i18n keys template-resolver.documentEditor.images, template-resolver.documentEditor.imagesVariable and templateResolver.errors.document.imagesBlockPdfOnly ship in de, es, fr and it.
  migration: Declare a template variable with type `images`, place the Images block, and pass FileRef ids of the record in `variables`. Images resolve only in the real PDF render, previews show placeholders. The ids must come from the record on the server, never from client input: a resolved id is read for the whole tenant without an entity access check.
  -->
- 0250376: actionForm can derive head totals from an embedded list
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: actionForm can derive head totals from an embedded list
  detail: An actionForm screen declares `derive` for head fields: sum, subtract, multiply, percent over other fields, or listSum over one cell of an embedded list with an optional whenEmpty fallback. The renderer recomputes them live and shows them read-only; a listSum without whenEmpty becomes an input while the list is empty. withFormDerivations(schema, screen) recomputes them on the server before validation, so client totals are never trusted; boot fails when the handler schema is not wrapped with the screen's own derive. A field that only feeds a `whenEmpty` fallback is read-only while the lists have rows. New embedded derived op `percent` (from[0] * from[1] / 100).
  migration: Add `derive` to the actionForm screen and wrap the handler schema with `withFormDerivations(schema, screen)`; new embedded derived op `percent`.
  -->
- a08f6d6: The tenant "Email sending" screen is a standard settings form. The provider is a select with "Platform sending (default)" and "Own SMTP server"; the SMTP fields sit in the same form with one save.
  
  A selector owner without panels now generates one configEdit screen `<owner>-tenant` instead of a dashboard around a dormant `<owner>-tenant-selection` form. The provider select gets an empty option for "no own provider", labelled by `<field label key>.platformDefault` or the generic `config.settings.provider.platformDefault`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Extension-selector settings form is one standard configEdit screen
  detail: Without owner panels the provider form is the `<owner>-tenant` screen itself (no dashboard, no `<owner>-tenant-selection`). The provider select offers an empty "platform default" option next to the plugin ids.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: mail-foundation
  type: improvement
  title: Email sending offers a platform default and an own SMTP server
  detail: The provider field is labelled "Send via" with the options "Platform sending (default)" (empty, saved as "") and "Own SMTP server"; the SMTP fields show only while the own server is picked.
  -->
- 6352d97: The pre-push shim no longer executes a `kumiko-pre-push` from an untrusted ancestor. The upward walk ends at `$HOME` (inclusive) and skips ancestors owned by another user or writable by group or others, such as `/tmp`.
  
  `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/search` exports `collectSearchableFieldNames` and `configureTenantSearchIndex`, so apps stop copying the per-tenant index setup. `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-server-runtime` exports `diskFileRoute`, an anonymous GET route that serves allowlisted disk files with ETag and 304. `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer/flow-diagram` exports `renderFlow` and the `FlowSpec` types for static animated SVG flow diagrams.
  
  Stock caps reserve atomically under a per-tenant advisory lock, so two parallel writes can no longer both pass the cap. The document designer ships its own stylesheet, disables Upload when the files feature is not mounted, and disables the test mail with a hint when the server cannot resolve an address (new `send-test-status` query).
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: fix
  title: Pre-push shim skips untrusted ancestors and stops at $HOME
  detail: The shim walked up to / and could exec a kumiko-pre-push planted in /tmp or another shared directory. The walk now ends at $HOME and skips ancestors that another user owns or that group or others can write to.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Search index setup helpers
  detail: collectSearchableFieldNames(registry) returns the deduplicated searchable fields of all entities and configureTenantSearchIndex(adapter, registry, tenantId) configures a tenant index with them, both exported from the search entry.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: diskFileRoute for allowlisted disk files
  detail: diskFileRoute({ path, resolveFile }) returns an anonymous GET extra route with a :file parameter. resolveFile maps the raw name to a disk path or null for 404; the file is served with mime type, ETag and 304 handling.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer
  type: improvement
  title: flow-diagram subpath
  detail: "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer/flow-diagram" exports renderFlow(spec) and the FlowSpec, FlowNode, FlowEdge, FlowIcon types, a pure string function that renders an animated SVG flow diagram.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-counter
  type: fix
  title: Stock caps are atomic under parallel writes
  detail: withStockCap now takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock per tenant and cap, so concurrent creates cannot both pass the check and exceed the cap.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: improvement
  title: send-test-status query for the template test mail
  detail: template-resolver:query:send-test-status answers whether a test mail can be sent (canSend) and, if not, why (no_channel or no_address), so clients can disable the action instead of failing on send.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: document-designer
  type: improvement
  title: Stylesheet export for the designer
  detail: "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-document-designer/web/styles.css" registers the designer's own Tailwind sources. Apps that embed the designer import it after the renderer stylesheet.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: document-designer
  type: fix
  title: Upload and test mail follow the server's capabilities
  detail: Upload is disabled with a hint when the files feature is not mounted, and the test mail button is disabled with a hint when the server has no email channel or no address for the user.
  -->

  type: breaking
  title: Renderer stylesheet no longer scans the document designer
  detail: The renderer stylesheet stopped scanning the document designer sources by relative path, which broke in isolated installs.
  migration: Apps that embed the document designer add `@import "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-document-designer/web/styles.css";` after the renderer stylesheet import in their styles.css.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: TenantDb.advisoryXactLock
  detail: ctx.db.advisoryXactLock(namespace, key) takes a transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed on the handle's own tenantId plus key, so tenants never contend and the caller cannot pick another tenant. It needs no unsafeRaw grant.

The migration splitter and the replay parser handle dollar-quoted bodies, RENAME, CREATE TABLE AS and DO blocks. A new guard flags `unsafeAppendEvent` outside migrations, upcasters and tests.

  feature: types

SharedContextFields gains configAccessorFactory; _configAccessorFactory stays as a deprecated alias. dbOutsideTransaction stays TenantDb | undefined (undefined only in the member-resolution and before-transaction denial phases and in platform-metering tenant mode); hasOutsideTransactionDb(ctx) narrows it and requireOutsideTransactionDb(ctx) throws when it is missing.
  migration: Replace ctx.outsideTransaction(fn) with runInOwnTransaction(ctx.dbOutsideTransaction, fn). Read configAccessorFactory instead of _configAccessorFactory.

  migration: Drop _userId from hand-built JobContext objects (tests, job helpers) and replace reads of ctx._userId with SYSTEM_USER_ID. Known hits - money-horse data-export integration test, offlot-app channel-text generate-texts.job.ts.

## 0.374.0

### Minor Changes

- 40b8667: actionForm successLinks and resetOnSuccess, field placeholder
  
  An `actionForm` takes `successLinks` (`{ screen, idFrom?, label }[]`, exclusive with `redirect`): after a successful submit the screen stays and shows the success box (`successMessage`, default "Done.") with one link per entry. Targets resolve like `redirect`; the id comes from the handler's success payload, and a link to a record screen without a string id is hidden. `idFrom` is required for a record target (`entityEdit`, `projectionDetail`) and optional for a list, dashboard or form target, which opens without an id; boot rejects a record target without `idFrom`. `resetOnSuccess: true` resets the form to its initial values after a successful submit while the screen stays put. The box disappears with the next edit or submit.
  
  `EditFieldSpec.placeholder` (i18n key, literal as fallback) sets the empty-input hint of single-line text, number and textarea fields on every screen type with edit fields; other field kinds ignore it.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: actionForm successLinks and resetOnSuccess
  detail: successLinks keeps the actionForm open after a successful submit and lists links resolved like redirect; boot rejects it together with redirect, with an unknown target or with a record target without idFrom. resetOnSuccess clears typed values after success. Role projection drops links to screens the role cannot reach.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer
  type: improvement
  title: Success box with links, form reset and field placeholder
  detail: The actionForm success box shows the default text "Done." (kumiko.actionForm.success) next to successMessage links, resetOnSuccess remounts the form with its initial values, and EditFieldSpec.placeholder reaches text, number and textarea inputs.
  -->
- de5d674: clientAction row actions backed by a client registry
  
  A row action with `kind: "clientAction"` runs a function from a client bundle instead of a write handler. The schema carries `action: "<feature>:<kebab>"`; a client feature registers the function under `ClientFeatureDefinition.clientActions` (merged like `columnRenderers`, last wins with a warning). The handler gets the payload (default `{ id: row.id }`, or the `payload` extractor) and returns `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, message }`. Success shows a toast (`successMessage`, default "Done.") and refetches, a failure shows an error toast, and a throw or an unregistered name shows a generic one and logs the name. `confirm`, `confirmLabel`, `style: "danger"`, `visible`, `icon` and `display` work as on a write handler; `redirect` and `rowClick` do not exist. Toolbar actions do not take it. Boot rejects a name that is not `<feature>:<kebab>`.
  
  auth-email-password registers `auth-email-password:request-password-reset` and `auth-email-password:request-email-verification`, both taking `{ email }`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: clientAction row actions
  detail: RowAction gains kind "clientAction" with a client-registered handler name; boot rejects a name that is not <feature>:<kebab>, and the surface keys include its confirm, confirmLabel and successMessage.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer
  type: improvement
  title: Client action registry for row actions
  detail: ClientActionsProvider, ActionNoticeProvider and runClientAction execute clientAction row actions on list, related list and record actions, with confirm, toast feedback and refetch.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer-web
  type: improvement
  title: ClientFeatureDefinition.clientActions
  detail: Client features register clientAction handlers; createKumikoApp merges them and shows their outcome as toasts.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: improvement
  title: Client actions for password reset and email verification
  detail: emailPasswordClient registers auth-email-password:request-password-reset and auth-email-password:request-email-verification for clientAction row actions.
  -->
- 47e3a05: Dashboard screen panels get a fallback, new static text panel
  
  A dashboard `screen` panel takes `fallback` (same-feature short id or `<feature>:screen:<id>`): when `visibleWhen` is unmet or its gate query fails, that screen is embedded in the panel's place, with the same `label` and `chromeless`. While the gate loads nothing renders. The boot validator requires `visibleWhen` for it, resolves the target like the panel's own screen and rejects a target that has its own `visibleWhen`. Extension-selector owner panels qualify a short `fallback` like `screen`, and a role without access to the fallback screen gets the panel without it.
  
  The new `text` panel (`DashboardTextPanel`) renders static `blocks`: `heading`, `paragraph` (`emphasis` muted or strong), `list`, `code` (verbatim, scrollable) and `hint`. `text` and list items are i18n keys and are checked as required translation keys; `visibleWhen`, `span` and an optional `label` work as on other panels.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer-web
  type: improvement
  title: Screen-panel fallback and static text panel
  detail: A dashboard screen panel embeds its fallback screen when visibleWhen is unmet or the gate query fails (nothing while loading). The new text panel renders heading, paragraph, list, code and hint blocks from i18n keys, without markdown or HTML.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Boot validation for screen-panel fallback and text panels
  detail: DashboardScreenPanel.fallback needs visibleWhen and a registered, embeddable target without its own visibleWhen. DashboardTextPanel (kind "text", exported with DashboardTextBlock) rejects empty blocks and empty lists; its text keys are required translation keys. Extension-selector panels qualify a short fallback ref, and role projection drops a fallback the role cannot reach.
  -->
- 926e08e: Dashboards bound to a record, with header actions, auto refresh and relative times
  
  `DashboardScreenDefinition.record: { param, payloadKey?, query?, titleField? }` ties a dashboard to one record via a URL search param. The id is merged into every panel and `visibleWhen` gate query after `filter`/`timeRange` and before a panel's own `params`; screen-kind panels get none. Without the param the dashboard shows a hint (`kumiko.dashboard.record.missing`) and runs no query. `record.query` loads the record row for the page title (`titleField`), the actions and `refresh.field`.
  
  `actions` puts writeHandler, navigate and clientAction actions in the dashboard header, running on the record row (or `{ id, [payloadKey]: id }` without `record.query`). After a success the record and all panels refetch. The header bar is the shared `HeaderActionsBar` component also used by projectionDetail. Boot rejects actions without `record`, drawer actions, `rowClick` and `redirect`.
  
  `refresh: { seconds } | { field }` polls the record and all panels, never faster than 5 s (`DASHBOARD_MIN_REFRESH_SECONDS`): boot rejects `seconds` below it, a `field` value is clamped at runtime. A running refetch is never stacked and polling stops on unmount.
  
  `valueFormat: { kind: "relativeTime" }` on stat panels and `{ kind: "relativeTime", atMs }` as a text param render epoch ms via `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` in the user locale ("5 minutes ago", "in 30 seconds") and keep ticking while mounted.
  
  fillAction is only allowed on text, number, decimal and bigInt fields and rejected on password, sensitive and writeOnly ones; an actionForm `load` never fills those fields from the loaded record. The email clientActions answer a 429 with the new `auth.errors.tooManyRequests` instead of the login-specific rate-limit text.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Dashboard record binding, header actions, refresh and relative time
  detail: Dashboards take record, actions and refresh; stat panels and text params gain a relativeTime format; the surface keys include kumiko.dashboard.record.missing.
  -->

  detail: DashboardValueFormat is now a union of DashboardCurrencyFormat and DashboardRelativeTimeFormat. Stat panels take both, chart panels only the currency one, and boot rejects relativeTime on a chart.
  migration: A chart panel that declares valueFormat keeps working with { kind: "currency", currency }. Code that types a chart's valueFormat as DashboardValueFormat should use DashboardCurrencyFormat instead; relativeTime on a chart was never meaningful and now fails boot.
  -->
- 1d72366: Derived list searchability, actionForm load, drawer rowClick
  
  A projectionList over an entity-convention list query whose entity has no searchable field derives `searchable: false` (no search box, no whitelist entry needed); declaring `searchable: true` there fails boot. `ActionFormScreenDefinition.load` (`{ query, idParam? }`) seeds the form from a query keyed by the record id; with `load` no URL param, drawer param or handoff value reaches the form. A `drawer` row action takes `rowClick: true` like `navigate` does, in lists and relatedList sections, and counts toward the one-rowClick limit.

  -->
- c3df9a2: Field prefix, suffix and fill action
  
  `EditFieldSpec` takes `prefix` and `suffix` (an i18n key with the literal as fallback, or `{ field }` for the live value of another form field) and `fillAction` (`{ label, query, field, params? }`). The affixes render beside single-line text and number inputs. The fill button runs `query` with the form values picked by `params` and writes `result[field]` (string or number) into the field, which makes the form dirty and submits the value even on a `readOnly` field. A failed query or a result of another type shows an error under the field.

  feature: framework
  type: improvement

  detail: Boot fails when a fillAction query is not a registered query handler, or when a { field } affix or a fillAction params source is not a field of the same form.
  -->

  detail: Text and number inputs show prefix and suffix text, and a fillAction renders a button that fetches a suggestion into the field, also for a readOnly field. The Input primitive takes prefix, suffix and fill; renderer-web draws them beside the input.
  -->
- 1b710f1: pagedListSchema and pageRows for in-memory projectionList queries, tenant-caps:list pages by offset
  
  `pagedListSchema(sortableFields)` is the query schema for a projectionList whose rows are merged in memory: `limit`, `offset`, `search`, `sort` (enum of the sortable fields), `sortDirection` and `totalCount`. `pageRows(rows, request, { searchFields, defaultSort })` searches case-insensitively, sorts (missing values last, ties by `id`), slices by `offset` and `limit`, and returns a `CursorResult` with `nextCursor: null` and `total` only when `totalCount` is set.
  
  `cap-overview:query:tenant-caps:list` now uses them. The projectionList pager sends `offset` and never a cursor, so every page used to show page 1. The query no longer pages by `cursor`: a caller that still sends one gets a 400 validation error instead of page 1 (`pagedListSchema` rejects `cursor`). An unknown `sort` is rejected by the schema.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: pagedListSchema and pageRows for in-memory list queries
  detail: pagedListSchema(sortableFields) and pageRows(rows, request, { searchFields, defaultSort }) cover search, sort (missing values last, ties by id), offset paging and an optional total for projectionList queries over merged rows. PagedListRequest and PagedListRowValue are exported; nextCursor is always null.
  -->

  feature: cap-overview
  type: breaking
  title: tenant-caps:list pages by offset and rejects cursor
  detail: The cap overview list showed page 1 on every page because the pager sends offset and the query only read cursor. tenant-caps:list now takes offset like the pager; a cursor in the payload is rejected with a 400 validation error and sort is an enum of the sortable fields. The unused cap-overview.errors.invalidCursor and sortFieldUnsupported keys are gone.
  migration: Callers of cap-overview:query:tenant-caps:list must send offset instead of cursor, and only a sortable field name as sort. Apps that override the removed i18n keys cap-overview.errors.invalidCursor or cap-overview.errors.sortFieldUnsupported can delete them. No caller in the kumiko-enterprise, kumiko-platform, kumiko-studio or app repos sends a cursor or defines these keys.
  -->
- 8e735ed: progress-list rows take used/limit, an unlimited state and a danger tone
  
  A `progress-list` row may return `used` and `limit` (`number | null`) instead of `value` and `fraction`. The panel shows "used / limit" with the viewer's number format and fills the bar with `used / limit`. `limit: null` shows "used / unlimited" without a bar. The new row field `tone` (`DashboardProgressTone`: `"default" | "danger"`) colors bar and value; used/limit rows turn `danger` automatically once `used >= limit`, and an explicit `tone` wins. `ProgressListRow.fraction` accepts `null` (no bar) and gains `tone`. New translation key `kumiko.dashboard.progress.unlimited` in the defaults and the de, es, fr and it bundles.

## 0.373.0

### Minor Changes

- 6913834: `loadPendingFileRef` and `bindPendingFileRef` for custom handlers
  
  `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/files` exports two helpers for handlers that create their own record from an uploaded file. `loadPendingFileRef({ fileRefId, entityName, fieldName, user, db })` returns `{ id, storageKey, mimeType, size, version }` of the caller's own unbound upload for that field, or `undefined` for a foreign, bound, deleted or wrong-field fileRef. `bindPendingFileRef({ ..., entityId })` binds it with the stream version and returns `"bound"`, `"not-pending"` or `"version-conflict"` (a parallel bind lost the race). It applies the same ownership check as the save pipeline. Anonymous callers never own an upload, so both helpers treat them as having none. The helper does not check write access to `entityId`; the handler must already be allowed to write that record.
  
  `loadFileRefRows` now reads stream versions before the rows, so a bind that commits in between makes the second update conflict instead of overwriting the first.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: loadPendingFileRef and bindPendingFileRef bind a caller's own pending upload from a custom handler
  detail: Additive. fileName is not part of PendingFileRef because it is personal data; read it via the fileRef executor's detail. Unexpected update errors throw; version_conflict and unique_violation map to "version-conflict".
  -->
- 6913834: A handler can declare several rate-limit buckets
  
  `rateLimit` accepts a list: `rateLimit: [{ per: "user", limit: 2, windowSeconds: 3600 }, { per: "tenant+handler", limit: 3, windowSeconds: 3600 }]`. Each bucket applies on its own, and the check is all-or-nothing: if one bucket is exhausted the call answers 429 for that bucket and none of them is charged. `additionalRateLimits` (payload buckets) gets the same all-or-nothing check.
  
  All-or-nothing holds within one list. Handler `rateLimit` buckets are charged in the pre-handler gate, before schema validation; payload buckets (`additionalRateLimits`) need the validated payload. A later payload rejection therefore does not undo the handler charges.
  
  `RateLimitResolver` has a new required method `enforceAll(requests)` that checks and deducts several buckets atomically (one Lua script in the Redis resolver). Boot fails for an empty list, for the same `per` twice, for the same `payloadField` twice in `additionalRateLimits`, and for anonymous handlers with a user-keyed bucket or tenantless-anonymous handlers with a non-ip bucket in the list. `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/handlers` exports `RateLimitOptions`, `declaredRateLimitOptions` and `isRateLimitOption`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: rateLimit accepts a list of buckets that are enforced all-or-nothing
  detail: RateLimitDeclaration is now a single option, a non-empty list of options or the disabled form. RateLimitResolver gains the required method enforceAll(requests: readonly RateLimitBucketRequest[]); createRateLimitResolver and createUnlimitedRateLimitResolver implement it. Payload buckets in additionalRateLimits are charged through the same call.
  migration: Custom RateLimitResolver implementations and test fakes need an enforceAll method (check every bucket, then deduct from all or none, and throw RateLimitError for the rejected bucket with the largest retryAfter). Existing rateLimit declarations stay valid. A duplicate payloadField in additionalRateLimits is now a boot error; merge the entries into one.
  -->

## 0.372.0

### Minor Changes

- a4401ab: `kumiko check` honours the boot-validator options declared in kumiko.config.ts
  
  The boot step of `kumiko check` ran `validateBoot` without the options the app passes to `runProdApp`, so allowlisted or exempted navs still warned there. `defineAppConfig` now takes an optional `validateBootOptions` (`navAllowlist`, `navAllowlistExempt`, `warnOnUniqueAccessRoles`; `env` and the cipher stay runner-owned). The managed `kumiko/schema.ts` exports it as `VALIDATE_BOOT_OPTIONS`, `kumiko check` and `kumiko-schema validate` hand it to `validateBoot`, and a wrong shape fails the boot step with a clear message. New apps pass the same options from their `bin/main.ts` and `bin/server.ts` to `runProdApp` and `runDevApp`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: kumiko check validates the boot configuration with the validateBootOptions from kumiko.config.ts
  detail: Set validateBootOptions in defineAppConfig (navAllowlist, navAllowlistExempt, warnOnUniqueAccessRoles); the managed kumiko/schema.ts exports it as VALIDATE_BOOT_OPTIONS and kumiko check validates with it. Apps with a hand-written kumiko/schema.ts can export VALIDATE_BOOT_OPTIONS themselves.
  migration: Existing apps get the new line in kumiko/schema.ts through `kumiko-upgrade --apply` (managed file). The bin files belong to the app: pass `...(appConfig.validateBootOptions && { validateBootOptions: appConfig.validateBootOptions })` to runProdApp in bin/main.ts and to runDevApp in bin/server.ts (import appConfig from "../kumiko.config") so runtime and kumiko check agree.
  -->
- 236858e: `executor.detail()` and `executor.list()` return the entity's row type
  
  `createEntityExecutor(name, entity)` and `createEventStoreExecutor(table, entity, options)` now return `EventStoreExecutor<EntityRow<E>>`. `detail` resolves to `EntityRow<E> | null` and `list` to `CursorResult<EntityRow<E>>`, so `row.title` needs no cast or schema parse. `EntityRow<E>` is exported from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db` and follows what the executor returns at runtime: money is one `{ amount, currency, amountScaled, amountMinor }` key, a located timestamp one `{ at, tz, utc }` key, `date` is a `Temporal.PlainDate`, `timestamp` and `insertedAt` are `Temporal.Instant`, soft-delete keys are required only when `softDelete` is the literal `true`, and bigInt and jsonb stay `unknown`. A wide `fields` map falls back to `Record<string, unknown>`. Create and update payloads stay untyped, and a typed executor is still assignable to the untyped `EventStoreExecutor`.
  
  `createBooleanField` is now typed as non-null (`default: boolean`), matching what it stores.
  
  Breaking: a `row as T` cast whose target the row type no longer overlaps becomes a compile error, and casts that still compile but are now redundant can go. Run the codemod first, then fix what it lists as manual.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: executor.detail() and executor.list() return EntityRow<E>, derived from the entity definition
  detail: Rows of createEntityExecutor / createEventStoreExecutor are typed per entity; wide entities keep Record<string, unknown>. createBooleanField is typed non-null. UserMfaRow in the bundled auth-mfa feature now declares enabledAt and lastUsedAt as Temporal.Instant, which is what the row always held.
  migration: Remove the `row as T` casts on executor.detail() / executor.list() results with `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply` (codemod remove-engine-payload-casts). Casts to a type the row does not satisfy stay and are listed as manual; replace them with a field-level check or a narrower type.
  codemod: scripts/codemod/remove-engine-payload-casts.ts
  manualAfterCodemod: true
  -->
- 27b759f: Orphaned upload bytes are swept
  
  Bytes written by `POST /files`, `createFileRefFromBytes`, `uploadFileBytesBeforeTransaction` and the seed `createFileRef` are recorded in the new `store_file_upload_ledger` table before they reach storage. The commit that creates the fileRef row removes the ledger row in its own transaction. The new hourly `files:job:sweep-orphaned-uploads` job deletes the bytes (original and derivatives) of uploads still unclaimed after `uploadSweepGraceHours` (default 24, minimum 1; option of `createFilesFeature`). A commit that arrives after its upload was swept fails with `upload expired`. Plain `files.ref(key).write()` stays untracked and is never swept.
  
  `FileContext` gains `writeUploadBytes` and `forgetUploadBytes`, `FileProviderResolver` may carry `uploadLedgerFor`, and `TenantDb.deleteMany` now returns the number of deleted rows. Build a tenant's `FileContext` with `createTenantFileContext(resolver, tenantId)` so it carries the resolver's ledger.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: files
  type: breaking
  title: Orphaned upload bytes are swept through a new upload ledger
  detail: The files feature registers the store_file_upload_ledger table and an hourly sweep job. FileContext has the new methods writeUploadBytes and forgetUploadBytes, which the four upload paths use; a custom FileContext or resolver must provide the ledger (withUploadLedger wraps a resolver). TenantDb.deleteMany resolves to the number of deleted rows instead of void. A fileRef commit whose ledger row was already swept throws InternalError "upload expired".
  migration: Generate and apply a migration with `kumiko-schema generate` — uploads fail without the new store_file_upload_ledger table
  -->
- 221f81c: JWT verification drops the `system` and `all` roles
  
  A token signed with the right key could carry `roles: ["system"]` and be treated as the in-process System identity. `verify()` now removes `system` and `all` from the roles claim; minting never grants them. `anonymous`, `SystemAdmin` and all other roles are kept. The test request helper (`stack.http.*`) now throws when handed a user with the `system` role; use `stack.dispatcher.write/query` for system calls.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Tokens carrying system or all lose those roles on verify
  detail: jwt.verify strips the system and all roles that session minting never grants, so a self-signed or leaked-key token cannot act as System.
  migration: Apps that mint their own tokens with the `system` role must stop doing so and use `createSystemUser` or system dispatch in-process instead. Tokens issued by the framework are unaffected. Tests that send a system user over `stack.http.*` must switch to `stack.dispatcher.write/query`.
  -->
- dca222d: HTTP spans and metrics use the route pattern instead of the raw request path
  
  The `http.route` span attribute and the `route` label on `kumiko_http_requests_total` and `kumiko_http_request_duration_seconds` now carry the matched route pattern (`/api/heartbeat/:token`), or `unmatched` when no route matched. Raw paths put path-param secrets into traces and gave every id its own metric series. The span is named `GET /api/heartbeat/:token` instead of `http.request`, and the `http.target` attribute is gone.
  
  `observabilityOptions` (`BaseEntrypointOptions`, `RunProdAppOptions`, `RunWorkerAppOptions`) is deprecated and has no effect anymore: it only configured query-string redaction, and the route label carries no query string. `ServerOptions.observabilityOptions` is removed.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: http.route and the metric route label carry the route pattern, http.target is removed
  detail: Spans are named "METHOD pattern" instead of "http.request"; paths no route matched are labelled "unmatched". The PII ciphertext guard message names the pattern as well.
  migration: Dashboards, alerts and trace queries keyed on raw paths or on the span name "http.request" must switch to route patterns and the "METHOD pattern" span name. Read the query string from your access logs if you relied on http.target.
  -->
- 2cb8b4f: `resolvePageHead` receives the request's preferred locales
  
  The resolver input gains `preferredLocales`: an ordered, canonicalized, deduplicated list with a valid `?lang=` first, then every Accept-Language tag by q (q=0 and malformed tags dropped, header order breaks ties). A resolver can walk it and use the first locale it has content for, instead of parsing the header itself. `runProdApp`, `runDevApp` and `hostDispatch` pages all pass it. `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/i18n` exports `rankAcceptLanguage` and `rankPreferredLocales`; `pickAcceptLanguage` behaves as before. With a page-head resolver configured, `runProdApp` HTML responses send `Vary: Host, Accept-Language`, so a shared cache keeps the locale variants apart.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: headless
  type: improvement
  title: resolvePageHead gets preferredLocales (?lang= first, then Accept-Language by q) so resolvers can pick a content locale
  detail: Callers constructing PageHeadResolveInput themselves must now pass preferredLocales (an empty array when no preference is known).
  -->

### Patch Changes

- de53a14: `createEntity` accepts inline field literals without `as const`
  
  `createEntity({ fields: { owner: { type: "reference", entity: "user" } } })` no longer collapses to `never`: the `fields` type parameter is `const`, so `type` keeps its literal instead of widening to `string`. Field helpers (`createTextField` and friends) behave as before.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: createEntity no longer collapses to never for inline field literals such as { type: "reference", entity }
  detail: The fields type parameter is const, so the literal type of each inline field survives without as const.
  -->
- 5cd8710: A save cannot name a file that is bound to another record
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: A save cannot reference a file that belongs to another record
  detail: Creating or updating a record with a file id that is already bound to a different record of the same tenant is now rejected with invalid_element on that field, the same error as for a foreign tenant. Pending uploads, ids the record already holds and moves between its own file fields are unaffected.
  -->
- 4224023: Seeds can call write handlers that declare a `rateLimit`
  
  The seed and seed-migration dispatcher of `runProdApp` had no `RateLimitResolver`, so any handler with a `rateLimit` failed with an internal error when a seed called it. Seeds now always run with `createUnlimitedRateLimitResolver()` (exported from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/pipeline`), even when the app has a real resolver: they are bootstrap writes, so they neither fail on a limit nor drain the buckets real requests use. Requests are limited as before.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: fix
  title: Seeds no longer fail on write handlers that declare a rateLimit
  detail: The seed dispatcher gets an unlimited RateLimitResolver instead of none; requests keep the app's resolver and limits.
  -->
- 9bc4bc4: Locked screens with a fallback stay in the schema of tenants without the feature
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: personal-access-tokens
  type: fix
  title: Tenants whose tier excludes API tokens now reach the lockedFallbackScreen
  detail: GET /api/schema removed every screen of a feature the tenant has switched off, and the role projection then dropped the navs of other features that pointed at them. The token list screen was gone, so the upgrade screen set via lockedFallbackScreen was never shown. Screens that declare a fallback (and the same-feature screens those fallbacks name) now stay in the schema; the server still rejects their queries and writes with feature_disabled, which makes the renderer show the fallback. Navs, content collections and workspaces of the disabled feature are still removed.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: personal-access-tokens
  type: improvement
  title: The token list looks like any other Kumiko list
  detail: The create button now sits in the page header next to the title, and an empty list shows the standard hint with a create button. The German title of the list screen is "API-Tokens" instead of "Personal Access Tokens", which also fixes the breadcrumb of the mint screen. Renderer, all apps: a projection list without an entity create button now shows its first primary toolbar action (one that needs no confirmation dialog) in the page header on desktop as well, with its label, instead of in the toolbar row; on phones it already did. On desktop only an icon derived from the action id (or declared on the action) is shown; the plus fallback exists only on phones. Consumers get this after the bump without code changes.
  -->

- 4a6e151: Relative imports name the TypeScript source file
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: import-extensions codemod and tsconfig options for .ts import specifiers
  detail: The import-extensions codemod rewrites relative import and export specifiers that end in .js or .jsx to the .ts or .tsx file next to the importer (import, export from, import type, import() and mock.module). It leaves a specifier alone and reports it when no such file exists. The framework repo itself now imports with .ts endings; its published dist is unchanged. tsc writes .js into the dist, and the .d.ts files keep .ts specifiers, which TypeScript resolves to the sibling .d.ts. An app tsconfig needs allowImportingTsExtensions: true, because the framework packages now ship sources with .ts specifiers and tsc checks them (the preset @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/tsconfig.app.json sets it). A tsconfig that emits JS also needs rewriteRelativeImportExtensions (TypeScript 5.7 or newer); a project that only type-checks code from another project reference needs rewriteRelativeImportExtensions false plus emitDeclarationOnly. Consumer code with .js endings keeps running once the option is set.
  migration: Add `allowImportingTsExtensions: true` to the app tsconfig (or extend @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/tsconfig.app.json), then run the codemod (bun node_modules/@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/src/scripts/codemod/import-extensions.ts . --write); the guard import-extensions reports remaining .js specifiers.
  codemod: scripts/codemod/import-extensions.ts
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement
  title: import-extensions guard reports relative .js and .jsx specifiers
  detail: The import-extensions guard fails on a relative specifier that ends in .js or .jsx in a .ts or .tsx file (import, export from, import type and import()). Declaration files and fixtures are skipped. The message points to the import-extensions codemod. There is no baseline.
  -->
- c051152: Managed files, kumiko.config.ts with defineAppConfig, script standard and port registry
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes

  detail: kumiko.config.ts default-exports defineAppConfig({ features, prodFeatures?, client: { entries }, ports: { dev, e2e, infra? } }). defineAppConfig throws on ports outside 1..65535, a port claimed twice within the app, an empty client.entries list and entries that leave the app. allAppFeatures(config) returns features plus prodFeatures. New exports @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/biome (Biome 2.5.7 preset with vcs.useIgnoreFile false) and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/tsconfig.app.json; an app's biome.json and tsconfig.json extend them and keep their own overrides next to extends.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: improvement
  title: Managed files: one template source for the scaffold, kumiko check managed and kumiko sync-managed
  detail: deploy/Dockerfile, deploy/Dockerfile.dockerignore, deploy/migrate-step.sh, .husky/pre-push, .github/workflows/{ci,release,cache-cleanup}.yml, the bunfigs and kumiko/schema.ts carry a kumiko-managed marker on line 1 (line 2 after a shebang or # syntax= line). kumiko new app writes them, plus kumiko.config.ts, bin/server.ts (was bin/dev.ts), bin/env-schema.ts, e2e/_helpers and src/__tests__/_setup.ts; bunfig.ci.toml is gone. kumiko/schema.ts is generated from kumiko.config.ts. kumiko-init-deploy prints a deprecation notice and goes away in the next release. Release targets come from package.json#kumiko.deploy.namespace and .deployment (default: the app name).
  migration: Existing apps: add kumiko.config.ts with defineAppConfig, then run kumiko sync-managed (dry run), kumiko sync-managed --write --adopt for files that are identical or should follow the template, and mark deliberate deviations with "# kumiko-managed: local <reason>" on line 2. Until kumiko.config.ts calls defineAppConfig, kumiko check only warns about drift and missing scripts.
  -->

  type: improvement
  title: kumiko check gains the managed and scripts steps; new kumiko sync-managed and kumiko ports
  detail: kumiko check managed compares framework-owned files with the installed templates and prints a diff; files with a local marker are skipped and listed. kumiko check scripts requires dev, build, start, typecheck, lint, check, test, test:unit, test:integration, test:integration:ci, test:dom (with uiRoots), test:real, e2e, e2e:real, screenshots and prepare, and lists extras. Both steps fail only once the app calls defineAppConfig. kumiko check accepts step ids as positional filters (kumiko check managed scripts). kumiko sync-managed [--write] [--adopt] writes the templates; it never overwrites a file without marker unless --adopt is passed, never touches local files and refuses symlinked paths. kumiko ports [workspace-root] lists the ports of every app below the root and exits 1 on a collision. kumiko agent lint also checks prodFeatures.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: types
  type: breaking

Switching the provider swaps the fields at once; fields of a provider that is not selected are not saved. A selector owner's selection screen (`<owner>-tenant-selection`) now carries the plugins' config keys (field id `<owner>-<key>`) and secrets (field id `<plugin>-<key>`, listed in the new ConfigEditScreenDefinition.secretKeys) behind a visible condition on the provider field; the separate `<plugin>-tenant` and `<plugin>-tenant-secrets` screens and their dashboard panels are gone, and so is the `config.settings.saveProvider` label.   detail: |
    postgres-js is the only DB driver. createDbConnection takes one options object, is synchronous and accepts the new options ssl and onNotice. The Bun.SQL provider, createConnection, createPgConnection and DB_PROVIDER are removed. The query helpers (selectMany, insertOne, transaction, asRawClient, ...) keep their API and are now exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db. The `tx` handed to the transaction() callback is typed as DbTx (the postgres-js transaction handle it always was at runtime) instead of the Bun.SQL instance type; a helper that takes `db: DbConnection` and receives that tx needs `DbRunner` or `DbTx`.

Remove DB_PROVIDER from your env files.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework

  detail: |
    A `filter`/`filters` entry on a field with `find: "secret"`, `encrypted: true` or a personal-data annotation made hit count and `totalCount` a value oracle (a prefix oracle for legacy plaintext rows before the backfill). The list handler now answers 400 `validation_error` with a field issue `field_not_filterable` (path `filter.<field>`). The one exception is `op: "eq"` with a string on a personal field with `find: "exact"` or `"fuzzy"`, which matches through the blind index. A sort on such a field falls back to id order instead of failing. Unknown fields are still dropped and fields without read access still match nothing; both checks run first.
  
    The entityList boot validator rejects a screen `filter` the handler would reject.

- 39b5de4: `personal: { of, whenAbsent: "self" }` encrypts rows without an owner under the row's own record key, so a record-forget shreds them
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: whenAbsent "self" keys ownerless personal fields on the record instead of the tenant
  detail: |
    A personal field with a nullable owner can now declare `personal: { of: "ownerId", whenAbsent: "self" }` (entity fields and `defineEvent` piiFields). While the owner is empty, the value is encrypted under `record:<entity>:<id>`, the same subject as `personal: "self"` on events and `personal: { of: "id" }` on entities. `forget-subject` on that record then erases the value, its blind index and its search document; with `"tenant"` the value stayed readable until the tenant was destroyed. A row can mix subjects: the ciphertext names its key inline, so owner-keyed, tenant-keyed and record-keyed fields decrypt side by side.
  
    The boot validator accepts "self" next to "tenant" and rejects it on `idType: "serial"` entities, because a forget-subject request needs a UUID record id. Owner transitions behave as for "tenant": when an update assigns an owner (absent to X) the value moves from the record key to the user key; the created event stays record-keyed. The data-retention hardDelete also erases the record key of an ownerless "self" row; a row with an owner keeps its owner key.
  migration: |
    Switching an existing field from `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to `"self"` changes only new writes. Events and rows written earlier stay tenant-keyed (still readable) until the PII event backfill re-keys them. The backfill fingerprint is bumped (`owner-rekey-v2`), so the boot-time backfill runs one more full pass: tenant-keyed values of rows without an owner move under their record key, tenant-keyed values of rows with an owner still move under that owner. The pass rewrites event payloads in place through the existing backfill path and queues the affected projections for rebuild. Apps that run the backfill manually call `backfillEventPiiEncryption` with `resolveOwnerFromProjection: true, rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields: true`, then rebuild the projections. Values of a record forgotten earlier become `[[erased]]`. The re-key covers entity lifecycle events only: custom `defineEvent` piiFields that switch from `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to `"self"` keep their old events tenant-keyed.
  
    Old events are never reinterpreted at read time: an old created event of a row that got an owner later keeps its record key until a forget of that record, which erases it, while the later owner-keyed copies stay readable.
  -->
- 478ee1f: createTenantDb takes one options object, and HandlerContext/AppContext drop the internal _userId and _handlerType fields

The positional form createTenantDb(db, tenantId, mode, tracer, meter, signal, grants) keeps working as a deprecated overload and is removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.
  
    old -> new:
      createTenantDb(db, tenantId) -> createTenantDb({ db, tenantId })
      createTenantDb(db, tenantId, "system", tracer, meter, signal, grants) -> createTenantDb({ db, tenantId, mode: "system", tracer, meter, signal, grants })
  migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It rewrites positional calls (literal undefined arguments are dropped) and reports spread arguments, calls with more than seven arguments and uses of createTenantDb as a value (callback, .bind/.call/.apply) with file and line.
  codemod: scripts/codemod/tenant-db-options.ts
  -->

  detail: |

The caller identity is ctx.user.id. requireSecretsContext reads ctx._userId first and falls back to ctx.user.id, so passing a handler context to it keeps the same audit identity. Provider contexts (FileProviderContext, MailTransportContext, InboundMailContext) keep their own _userId. JobContext._userId is unchanged.
  migration: Replace ctx._userId with ctx.user.id in write/query handlers and hooks. Known sites: one file each in money-horse, offlot-app, phronexsis and kumiko-enterprise. _handlerType had no readers.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 133ef08: A version conflict in append() reports the real stream version and no longer aborts the surrounding transaction
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Append version conflicts carry currentVersion and no longer poison the transaction
  detail: |
    append() inserts with ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, aggregate_id, version) DO NOTHING and reads the stream version in the still-intact transaction. VersionConflictError gets an optional currentVersion, and custom writes (ctx.appendEvent, stream.append, appendEventInTenantDb) now answer 409 with the winner's version instead of -1, so a client can rebase. A missing predecessor reports the real stream version too.
  
    Behaviour change: a lost append race no longer raises a unique violation, so the outer transaction is not aborted (25P02). A handler that catches the VersionConflictError keeps writing and commits. Idempotency-key collisions still throw IdempotentAppendConflictError. Relies on READ COMMITTED, the Postgres default.
  -->

- 8a7d835: Renaming a notification type keeps user preferences and address opt-outs
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: Renaming a notification type keeps user preferences and address opt-outs
  detail: r.notification accepts renamedFrom, a list of former qualified names. Preferences and address opt-outs stored under a former name keep applying to the renamed notification, and a stored choice under the current name wins over one under a former name. New writes via setPreference and the unsubscribe and resubscribe handlers are stored under the current name, resubscribeAddress also lifts opt-outs under former names. Boot fails if an alias is a current notification name, is the wildcard, or is claimed by two notifications.
  -->
- 7053800: The registrar takes one object per call: r.writeHandler, r.queryHandler, r.entity, r.requires and r.hook lose their positional forms
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Registrar methods take a single object, positional calls throw at registration
  detail: |
    r.writeHandler, r.queryHandler, r.entity, r.requires and r.hook now take one object. The positional overloads are gone from the types and throw when the feature is defined, with a message that points at the codemod. The throw is removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.
  
    writeHandler (queryHandler is the same shape):
      before: r.writeHandler("order:archive", schema, handler, { access });
      after:  r.writeHandler({ name: "order:archive", schema, handler, access });
  
    hook (type picks the handler shape, target is a name, a list or { allOf }):
      before: r.hook("postSave", "order", handler, { escapeHatch });
      after:  r.hook({ type: "postSave", target: "order", handler, escapeHatch });
  
    entity and requires:
      before: r.entity("order", definition, { table: ordersTable });  r.requires("auth", "tenant");
      after:  r.entity({ name: "order", ...definition, backingTable: ordersTable });  r.requires({ features: ["auth", "tenant"] });
  
    registerEntityCrud is no longer exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine; call r.crud(name, entity, options) instead. The entity option { table } is now backingTable on the r.entity object and lands in the feature's entityTables, not in its entities. HookDefinition and EntityObjectDefinition are exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types. Hook definitions are checked per type: validation takes no escapeHatch, phase only exists on postSave and postDelete, and { allOf } is not accepted on preSave.
  migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It rewrites every positional r.writeHandler, r.queryHandler, r.entity, r.requires, r.hook and registerEntityCrud call to the object form. Calls it cannot resolve statically (a spread argument, a registrar that is not typed as FeatureRegistrar) are listed as manual work with file and line; rewrite those by hand.
  codemod: scripts/codemod/object-form.ts
  manualAfterCodemod: true
  -->
- 5df8e3a: GET /api/schema hides screens and navs of features the tenant has switched off
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: The app schema no longer lists screens, navs and workspaces of features a tenant has switched off
  detail: A feature declared with r.toggleable() that is off for the caller's tenant (tier engine or feature toggles) used to stay in the nav while all its handlers answered 403 feature_disabled. GET /api/schema now drops its screens, navs, content collections and workspaces for that tenant, and every action, redirect, nav parent and workspace member that pointed at them is removed too. Entities and translations stay. The response is cached per role set and per set of disabled features, so tenants with the same set share one ETag. Without an effectiveFeatures resolver nothing changes.
  -->
- 22b7f6e: selectMany supports column projection via SelectOptions.fields
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: selectMany supports column projection via SelectOptions.fields
  detail: SelectOptions gains fields, a list of entity field names. selectMany then selects only those columns instead of all of them. An empty list or a name that is not a column of the table throws.
  -->
- 7053800: kumiko-upgrade prints and returns a stable id for each pending manual step
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: kumiko-upgrade names each pending manual step by an id
  detail: Every pending manual step of kumiko-upgrade now has a stable id, derived from the release version and the step title. The text output shows it in brackets and the JSON output carries it as manualId, so a script or an agent can tell steps apart and record which ones it has done.

## 0.365.1

### Patch Changes

- 93e1a7d: App and worker boot wait for Postgres instead of crashing
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: App and worker boot wait for Postgres instead of crashing
  detail: runProdApp and worker processes now probe the database before the schema-drift check and retry with exponential backoff (1s to 15s, up to 90s) on transient connection errors such as too_many_connections or ECONNREFUSED. The KMS health check at boot retries the same way. Non-transient errors like auth failures still abort immediately.
  -->
- 9a8abc9: eraseKey tombstones never-keyed subjects
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: crypto-shredding
  type: fix
  title: eraseKey leaves a tombstone for subjects that never had a key
  detail: eraseKey now records an erased entry even when the subject has no key (pre-KMS plaintext). A later createKey or write for that subject fails with subject_erased instead of minting a fresh key and re-encrypting the plaintext. Erase flows must write with writePurpose erasure after eraseKey. kumiko_subject_keys now gets one tombstone row per forgotten record subject and per step dispatch. The tenant destruction stage tenant-row now fails loudly when marking the tenant destroyed does not succeed.
  migration: Run backfill-pii before erasing Pre-KMS data, otherwise untouched plaintext stays readable after eraseKey.
  -->
- 34530bf: restore no longer fails on entities with money fields
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Restoring a soft-deleted row with a money field no longer fails with a 500
  detail: restore() wrote the raw stored row (money as bigint minor units) into payload.previous, and the jsonb bind threw. It now builds previous in the same domain form as delete(), so the restored event carries { amount, currency, ... } for money fields.
  -->
- 8633239: step-dispatcher delivers through a BullMQ job
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: step-dispatcher
  type: fix
  title: step-dispatcher delivers each dispatch as a retried job, so a slow receiver no longer delays other tenants
  detail: The step-dispatcher projection now only enqueues one `step-dispatcher:job:deliver` job per dispatch request, and the job performs the webhook or mail delivery. Redis holds only the dispatch stream id and the tenant, never the request payload. Transient failures (network error, timeout, 5xx, 408, 429, any mail adapter failure) are retried 3 times with exponential backoff; the outcome event and the payload key erase follow after the final attempt. Permanent failures (invalid url, blocked host, other 4xx, unavailable auth secret) are recorded at once. At most 2 deliveries per tenant run at the same time, so one tenant's slow receivers cannot hold up the others. This corrects the 0.346.0 note that a hanging receiver no longer stalls the dispatcher for every tenant: the shared consumer still delivered one request at a time.
  migration: step-dispatcher now needs a job runner (Redis) and a worker consuming the default worker lane. Without a job runner the projection throws instead of delivering. Test stacks must pass `jobs` to setupTestStack and call `drainJobs()` after the event dispatcher ran. `r.job` accepts `maxPerTenant: { limit, onLimit: "defer", deferMs? }`; a plain number still drops excess enqueues. A `webhook.send` request that gets a retryable status (5xx, 408, 429) is now sent up to 4 times under the same Idempotency-Key. Worker pods must know the deliver job before the projection enqueues it, so deploy worker and API together or the worker first. A dev server only consumes jobs when the app mounts `createJobsFeature()`.
  -->
- 34530bf: version_conflict reports the real stream version
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: version_conflict from delete, restore, forget and update reports the actual stream version
  detail: After a lost append race, delete, restore and forget returned currentVersion -1 and update returned the version read before the race, so expectedVersion and currentVersion looked equal. They now look up the stream version after the conflict; -1 remains only when that lookup fails.
  -->

- Updated dependencies [34530bf]

  - @cosmicdrift/kumiko-http@0.365.1

### Minor Changes

  title: Job handlers get ctx.metricsFor like request handlers
  detail: JobContext now exposes ctx.metricsFor(featureName) with the same contract as HandlerContext, so shared code can count under one stable feature name from jobs too. Unregistered names stay a silent no-op.
