### Patch Changes

- cd16f29: ctx.forTenant is available read-only in the beforeTransaction phase
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: ctx.forTenant is available read-only in the beforeTransaction phase
  detail: A beforeTransaction phase can now resolve ctx.forTenant(tenantId) for its own tenant and, as a SystemAdmin, for a foreign tenant, to read rows or build tenant-scoped inputs such as uploads. The returned db denies every write; a foreign tenant stays gated by the SystemAdmin check. reserveBeforeTransaction, perCommand and in-transaction handlers are unchanged.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: Migration notes for boot checks that were released as fixes
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Boot checks from the review round 1 release reject configurations that used to boot
  detail: |
    These checks shipped as fixes without migration notes. Each one throws for a configuration that was accepted before:
    - a where-rule subquery on a table whose columns cannot be derived
    - a drawer prefill that targets a sensitive field or a field the form does not render
    - two secret fields with the same id
    - access.personalData "public-intake" combined with rateLimit: { disabled: true }
    - a recordOwned field on an entity with idType "serial"
    - dedupeFeatures for same-named features with different registrations
    The agent-tools manifest check in buildToolCatalog throws when the catalog is built for a request, not at boot.
  migration: |
    Boot every app against the new version before rolling it out, and send one agent tool request if the app mounts agent-tools. Give where-rule subqueries a table with derivable columns, prefill only rendered non-sensitive fields, make secret field ids unique, give public-intake handlers a rateLimit that is not disabled, switch recordOwned entities to idType "uuid" or change the field's personal stance, and rename or align duplicated features.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: Several boot validations reject configurations that used to boot
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Boot rejects visibleWhen queries with required input, non-sql index where clauses, lockedWhen on read-restricted fields and same-named features with a different surface
  detail: |
    These checks used to be absent or silent and now stop the app at boot:
    - A screen or dashboard panel visibleWhen that names a query whose input schema does not accept an empty payload. The client gate runs it with an empty payload, so the screen stayed hidden.
    - An entity index where that is not a sql expression. It used to be dropped, which built a full (unique) index.
    - A lockedWhen field that declares access.read.
    - Two features with the same name whose screens, navs, jobs, events, translations, config keys, notifications, metrics or hooks differ. The second one used to be dropped.
  migration: |
    Boot each app once against the new version. For a visibleWhen query, make its input fields optional or point visibleWhen at an input-free query. Write index where clauses with sql`...`. Remove access.read from the lockedWhen field or lock on a field every role can read. Give differing same-named features distinct names or make their surfaces identical.
  -->
- 7aa3223: Bun.SQL provider parity
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Bun.SQL provider parity fixes for DB_PROVIDER=bun
  detail: Array params bind as Postgres array literals, transaction handles are detected correctly, Instant params are stored at millisecond precision, integer params reject fractions, and migrations hold their advisory lock on one pinned connection. LISTEN/NOTIFY uses Bun.SQL listen() on its own connection, which the pool idle timeout does not close, so the Bun provider no longer opens a postgres-js peer.

- 7e1b974: Console-spy tests only count the messages of the code under test

  title: Console-spy tests only count the messages of the code under test

  <!-- kumiko-changes

- fbc6938: Erasure writes store the erased sentinel instead of failing on a deleted subject key
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Executor update and delete with writePurpose erasure, and forget, write the erased sentinel for subjects whose key is gone
  detail: Re-encrypting a pre-KMS plaintext row after eraseKey threw subject-erased, so the erase flows could not finish their own follow-up writes. Update and delete with writePurpose erasure, and forget always, now replace the PII fields of an erased subject in changes and previous with the sentinel; fields of other subjects in the same row stay encrypted. Without writePurpose and for restore the subject-erased conflict stays. The forget-subject door close and the forget cleanup pass writePurpose erasure to the user lifecycle update.
  -->
- 5a1cdc1: Error docsUrl falls back to the framework page of the error code for uncovered app reasons
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Error docsUrl falls back to the framework page of the error code for uncovered app reasons
  detail: An error whose details.reason is an app reason not covered by errorDocs, such as the not_found reason of every NotFoundError, now carries docsUrl pointing at the framework page of its error code (for example /errors/not_found) instead of no docsUrl. Reasons covered by errorDocs keep the app link; framework reasons are unchanged.
  -->
- efa6253: Escape-hatch audit scope now covers streams until they finish
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Escape-hatch audits are collected for the whole stream
  detail: Dispatched streams run inside the escape-hatch audit scope for the full lifetime of the stream, and settled pending audits are dropped from the scope, so writes made while a stream is open are no longer missed.
  -->
- 80e2132: Erasure jobs delete the bytes of files that a tenant handover moved into the tenant
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Soft-delete cleanup and hardDelete retention delete the bytes of handed-over files
  detail: A tenant handover moves a fileRef row to the new tenant, but its storageKey keeps the previous tenant's prefix. The soft-delete cleanup and the data-retention hardDelete went through `ctx.files.ref()` and `ctx.files.list()`, which reject keys outside the job's tenant, so the bytes and derivatives of such files were never deleted and the soft-delete cleanup kept the row forever. Both now delete through the new `deleteFileRefBytes(files, row, context)` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/derivatives`, built on the new `FileContext.listFromFileRef(row)` (the row's key plus its derivatives, under the same trust as `refFromFileRef`). Form-draft discard deletes draft files through `refFromFileRef` as well.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: A file moved between file fields is disposed when it is later removed
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Removing a file that was moved to another file field of the same record deletes its fileRef
  detail: The fileRef stayed bound to the field it was first uploaded to. Once it was moved to a second field and then removed from that field, the dispose step skipped it and the file stayed readable. Dispose now accepts a binding to any file field of the same record.
  -->
- 82dc9a4: createAuthRoutes requires the switch-tenant MFA gate when MFA verify is wired
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: MFA verify without a switch-tenant gate fails at boot, and the gate result carries the session roles
  detail: createAuthRoutes throws when mfaVerifyHandler is set without switchTenantMfaGateHandler, and runDevApp and runProdApp check that the gate handler is registered before wiring, so a missing gate can no longer let switch-tenant skip MFA. The gate handler returns the roles with its clear result and the route mints the target session from them. assertRetiredCookieDomains is no longer exported, and the auth-session signup variant is composed from SignupOutcome. Setups that set mfaVerifyHandler must also register the switch-tenant gate handler.
  -->
- 82dc9a4: Write context fixes: stream version read, nested write serialization, ctx.notify through the query bridge
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: fetchForWriting reads one consistent stream version, nested ctx.write calls run in order, ctx.notify works through ctx.query
  detail: fetchForWriting derives the stream version from the same events it loads instead of a second read. Parallel ctx.write calls on one transaction are serialized, so a failing write rolls back only its own savepoint and no longer takes a concurrent successful write with it. ctx.notify called inside a handler reached through ctx.query is deferred onto the outer write's after-commit list instead of being delivered before that write commits. ctx.notify snapshots its options when it is called, so later mutation by the handler does not change the delivered notification. The JSDoc of AggregateStreamHandle.appendOne now states that it must not be mixed with other appends to the same aggregate in one handler.
  -->
- eef5ff1: Entity convention handlers: per-verb agent hints merge, foreign rows with a non-TenantId tenant fail loudly
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: registerEntityCrud merges per-verb agent hints into write.agent and read.agent
  detail: agents[verb] used to replace write.agent or read.agent wholesale, so write: { agent: { expose: true } } with agents: { delete: { risk: "high" } } dropped expose on delete. The two are now merged with the per-verb value winning. An escapeHatch update/delete/restore on a row whose tenantId is not a valid TenantId throws an InternalError instead of silently appending to the operator's own tenant stream.
  -->
- eef5ff1: Entity list and detail handlers with escapeHatch require SystemAdmin-only access
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Entity list and detail handlers with escapeHatch must declare SystemAdmin-only access
  detail: defineEntityListHandler, defineEntityDetailHandler and registerEntityCrud read options with escapeHatch now throw at definition unless access is { roles: ["SystemAdmin"] }, like write handlers already did. A cross-tenant read reachable by any tenant role leaked foreign rows.
  migration: Give every list/detail handler that declares escapeHatch access: { roles: ["SystemAdmin"] }, or drop the escapeHatch if the handler should stay tenant-scoped.
  -->
- 82dc9a4: File upload: projections run, failed uploads leave no row or blob, system files stay private
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Upload route creates the fileRef row in its own transaction, cleans up bytes on failure and excludes system files from unclaimedUploadReaders
  detail: The file routes and the API server use createProjectingTenantDb so projections on fileRef.created run. When the row insert or a projection throws, the upload route rolls the row back, deletes the stored bytes and answers 500. Files uploaded by the system user are no longer readable through unclaimedUploadReaders.
  -->
- eef5ff1: Job runner keeps its cron schedulers marked as seen and waits for an abandoned boot gate in stop()
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Cron schedulers of a running job runner survive orphan cleanup by an older runner, and stop() waits for a timed-out boot gate
  detail: The runner re-stamps its own cron schedulers in the orphan-cleanup seen hash every quarter of the grace period (one hset for all ids, cleared in stop()), so a mixed-version window longer than an hour no longer lets an older runner delete a scheduler a live runner holds. The stamps are written before the schedulers are upserted. A boot gate that exceeds its timeout is abandoned, not aborted: its handler keeps running, and stop() now waits for it (bounded) before closing connections.
  -->
- 82dc9a4: Handlers with additionalRateLimits fail at boot when no RateLimitResolver exists
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: buildServer throws at boot when a handler declares additionalRateLimits but no RateLimitResolver can be built
  detail: Without a Redis client or context.rateLimit every call to such a handler (auth-email-password signup and token requests, waitlist submit) answered 500 at request time. buildServer now throws at boot and names the handlers.
  migration: Wire a Redis client on context.redis (or pass context.rateLimit). For the waitlist without Redis, pass emailRateLimits: [].
  -->
- eef5ff1: PII backfill: explicit null owner is not a missing owner, owner re-key covers user-keyed values
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: PII backfill keeps ownerless events under the tenant key and re-keys values left under a previous owner
  detail: With resolveOwnerFromProjection the projection owner is now used only when the event does not carry the owner key at all; an explicit null owner resolves through whenAbsent like the live write path. The owner re-key stage (rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields) also moves user-keyed values to the projection's current owner when that is another user, so after an owner change X to Y that predates re-keying on transition, forgetting Y erases the value. Known divergence: a row that went ownerless, then owned by X, then ownerless again keeps its created-event value under the tenant key, while the live path keeps it with X.
  -->
- eef5ff1: pruneEvents accepts batchSize and handler contexts carry an after-commit notify factory
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: pruneEvents batchSize and _notifyAfterCommitFactory on the handler context
  detail: pruneEvents takes an optional batchSize that deletes the lowest event ids first, so callers can loop until deletedCount is below the batch size with one short transaction per batch. The handler context exposes _notifyAfterCommitFactory, a notify factory bound to the dispatcher's job runner for use after the transaction has committed.
  -->
- 2a33c8d: requireTierResolverPlugin replaces three copies of the tier-resolver build() check
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: requireTierResolverPlugin narrows a tier-resolver registration or fails the boot
  detail: requireTierResolverPlugin(usage) returns the TierResolverPlugin of a tenantTierResolver registration and throws "tier-resolver registration options must provide a build() factory" otherwise. runProdApp, the worker boot and runDevApp share it, so the boot error is identical in all three entry points.
  -->
- eef5ff1: Seed writes before their stream predecessor throw SeedTimeOrderError, checked inside the write transaction
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Back-dated seed writes fail with a typed SeedTimeOrderError
  detail: append() throws the exported SeedTimeOrderError (aggregateType, aggregateId, version, seedCreatedAt, predecessorCreatedAt) when a back-dated event would precede its stream predecessor, so seeders can tell it from other failures without parsing the message. The check now runs inside the insert transaction, so a concurrent live append can no longer land between check and insert.
  -->
- eef5ff1: kumiko-upgrade: --resolve refuses --dry-run, version detection handles prerelease pins and workspace members
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: kumiko-upgrade --resolve rejects --dry-run, and the installed version is found from workspace members and prerelease lockfile pins
  detail: kumiko-upgrade --resolve --dry-run used to write the marker anyway; it now exits with an error and writes nothing. The installed version is now looked up from the working directory up to the repo root (the first directory with .git or a package.json with workspaces), so running inside a workspace member of a hoisted-linker monorepo finds it, while a parent workspace outside the repo is still ignored. bun.lock pins like 0.364.0-next.1 resolve to their x.y.z core instead of being dropped.
  -->
- efa6253: An entity index where that is not a sql expression now throws
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Non-sql index where throws instead of building a full index
  detail: buildEntityTable no longer drops a malformed EntityIndexDef.where silently, which produced a full (unique) index that blocked reuse of soft-deleted values. moneyAmount is typed as a bigint column.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: Cron schedulers are restored after a failed seen stamp
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: A failed scheduler seen stamp at start no longer lets an older runner remove fresh cron schedulers for good
  detail: When the initial seen stamp failed, a concurrent older runner could delete the new runner's cron schedulers as orphans, and the periodic refresh only re-stamped them. The refresh now stamps and upserts the lane's cron schedulers again until both succeeded once.
  -->
- efa6253: A failing scheduler-seen stamp no longer stops the job runner start
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Job runner start survives a failed scheduler-seen stamp
  detail: The initial scheduler-seen stamp is best-effort like the periodic refresh and the orphan cleanup: a Redis error is logged as a warning and the runner still starts and registers its cron schedulers.
  -->
- efa6253: Boot validation rejects a lockedWhen field with a read restriction
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: lockedWhen on a field with access.read fails at boot
  detail: Roles that cannot read the lock field receive records without it, and the client then showed every record as locked. validateLockedWhen now rejects a lock field that declares access.read.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: moneyAmount is typed as a bigint column
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: moneyAmount returns ColumnBuilder<bigint> instead of ColumnBuilder<number>
  detail: The column was always created with bigint mode, so the driver returned a bigint while the type said number. The type now matches the runtime value. Code that assigned the column value to a number or did number arithmetic on it no longer typechecks.
  migration: Treat values read from a moneyAmount column as bigint (for example compare with 0n, or convert explicitly with Number() where the amount is known to fit). No schema change.
  -->
- a546703: The pdf-audit-export recipe uploads the PDF before the transaction
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: The pdf-audit-export recipe uploads the PDF before the transaction
  detail: The shipped pdf-audit-export example now renders and uploads the PDF in a beforeTransaction phase with uploadFileBytesBeforeTransaction and creates the fileRef row in the handler with createFileRefFromUploadedBytes, so the upload holds no pool connection. No runtime change.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: Correct the release note on .d.ts handling in the pii-personal-migration codemod
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: The pii-personal-migration codemod skips .d.ts files in migration mode too
  detail: An earlier release note said the codemod now skips .d.ts files in --report-stance mode. That mode already skipped them. What changed is that migration mode skips .d.ts files as well, matching --report-stance.
  -->
- efa6253: Read steps no longer warn about narrowed tenant filters for in/eq operator objects
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: No false narrowing warning for where.tenantId given as { in } or { eq }
  detail: The read.findOne and read.findMany steps unwrap operator-form tenant filters ({ in: [...] } and { eq }) before comparing them with the caller's tenant scope, and stay silent for operator forms they do not understand.
  -->
- 5c276e6: custom-handlers and tags-basic recipes follow the coding rules
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: custom-handlers and tags-basic recipes follow the coding rules
  detail: The custom-handlers recipe parses the detail row with Zod instead of casts and filters counter:active on the server (filter + totalCount) instead of in JS over one page. The tags-basic test isolates tests by tenant instead of raw DELETE statements. No runtime change.
  -->
- 21c5cbc: Recipe integration tests isolate per tenant instead of raw DELETE FROM resets
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Recipe integration tests isolate per tenant instead of raw DELETE FROM resets
  detail: The recipe integration tests that agents learn from no longer reset tables with raw DELETE FROM statements. Each test now runs in its own tenant with its own users, or uses unique ids. The kumiko-schema-check header comment is now English. No runtime change.
  -->
- fbc6938: Projection rebuild decrypts legacy PII ciphertext in file and image fields
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Rebuilding an entity with a personal file or image field no longer fails on ciphertext from old backfill events
  detail: The earlier PII backfill encrypted file and image uuid values in stored events. Replaying those created and updated events wrote the ciphertext into the uuid column and failed with invalid input syntax. applyEntityEvent now decrypts such values through the subject KMS, writes null for an erased subject, and throws a clear InternalError when no KMS is configured. Table rows were never affected because Postgres rejects the ciphertext on a uuid column.
  -->
- efa6253: Content-type resolution no longer labels SVG and HTML fragments as XML
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: SVG and HTML fragments are not resolved as application/xml
  detail: For uploads without a concrete content type, markup without an XML declaration is only treated as application/xml when its root element is not a known HTML or SVG element (namespace prefixes ignored). SVG logos and HTML snippets no longer route to XML ingest providers.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: restore reports an erased subject as a failure result
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: EventStoreExecutor.restore returns a subject_erased conflict instead of throwing
  detail: When the stored row has to be re-encrypted for a subject whose key was erased, restore now returns a failed WriteResult with the subject_erased ConflictError. The row stays soft-deleted and no restored event is appended. Code that called restore directly and caught the exception checks isSuccess instead.
  -->
- efa6253: Migration scan for retired framework tables understands more DROP/RENAME forms
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Retired-table scan handles DROP TABLE lists, schema-qualified names and RENAME
  detail: The scan of prior migrations for retired framework tables now marks every table in a DROP TABLE comma list as dropped, ignores a schema prefix such as "public"."table", and treats ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO as dropping the old and creating the new name.
  -->
- b6b75fa: Metric integer filters reject fractions and out-of-range values; feature-name constants exported
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: metrics
  type: fix
  title: Metric integer filters reject fractions and out-of-range values; feature-name constants exported
  detail: Filters on smallint, integer and bigint columns now fail validation for decimals and values outside the column range instead of a Postgres cast error. FILES_FEATURE and FILES_TENANT_DATA_FEATURE are exported and reused by compose-features.
  -->
- 0f8bff5: kumiko-schema status reports connection errors; kumiko-schema-check knows the scaffold layout
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: kumiko-schema status reports connection errors; kumiko-schema-check knows the scaffold layout
  detail: schema status now prints a one-line error with a hint and exits 1 when the database is unreachable or missing, instead of an uncaught stacktrace (the URL is never printed). kumiko-schema-check exits 0 with a pointer to kumiko-schema validate for apps whose kumiko/schema.ts derives ENTITY_METAS from APP_FEATURES. New scaffolds create the app database in docker-compose.
  -->
- 067aa7b: Seeds can create fileRefs through handlers that use createFileRefFromBytes
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: fix
  title: Seeds can create fileRefs through handlers that use createFileRefFromBytes
  detail: The seed dispatcher built its handler context without the file provider resolver, so a write handler invoked via systemWriteAs failed with "createFileRefFromBytes: ctx.files is unavailable". The seed context now carries the same file provider as the HTTP path.
  -->
- efa6253: Statutory system writes skip the select-option check; isUnchangedValue is shared with the form
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Retention and erasure writes skip the select-option rule
  detail: Framework system-user updates that name a writePurpose (retention, erasure) are no longer blocked by conditional select options. The null-clear comparison helper isUnchangedValue moved to engine/screen-helpers and is exported from ui-types so the renderer form and the executor share one definition.
  -->
- efa6253: A stream whose token expires mid-stream now fails with 401 `unauthenticated`
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Mid-stream token expiry returns 401 unauthenticated
  detail: A stream dispatched with a token that expires while the stream is open now ends with UnauthenticatedError (401) instead of AccessDeniedError (403), so clients show the session-ended hint. Access revocation mid-stream still returns 403 access_denied.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: TenantDb reads honour where.tenantId given as { in } or { eq }
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: A where.tenantId of { in: [...] } or { eq } narrows TenantDb reads instead of being ignored
  detail: TenantDb.readWhere only understood a plain id or an array. An operator form fell back to the full read scope (own tenant plus reference rows), so { in: [ownTenant] } still returned SYSTEM reference rows. It now unwraps { in } and { eq } with the same helper the read steps use for their narrowing warning. Ids outside the caller's scope are still dropped and never widen the read.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: Correct the tenantlessAnonymous release note about the tenant cookie
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: tenantlessAnonymous is blocked by an X-Tenant header only, not by the kumiko_tenant cookie
  detail: An earlier release note said a tenantlessAnonymous handler never runs when the client supplies X-Tenant or kumiko_tenant. Only the X-Tenant header blocks it. An ambient kumiko_tenant cookie does not, because the tenant resolver ignores the cookie on this path anyway.
  -->
- efa6253: setupTestStack rate-limit resolver uses the app-supplied redis
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Test-stack rate limiting follows appContext.redis when rateLimitNowMs is set
  detail: With rateLimitNowMs the test stack builds its own rate-limit resolver; it now uses the redis instance passed via the app context instead of always the internal test redis, so buckets prefilled or cleared through the app redis take effect.
  -->
- 72a5c9c: ZIP entry listing ignores fake end-of-central-directory records in the comment
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: The ZIP plausibility check picks the end record whose comment length reaches the end of the file
  detail: The scan took the last end-of-central-directory signature, so a signature inside the archive comment could point the check at forged entry names. A candidate now only counts when its offset plus 22 bytes plus its comment length equals the file length. A docx upload with bytes appended after the end record is therefore rejected as content_mismatch.
  -->

## 0.364.0

### Minor Changes

- e9b032f: Write handlers can run external calls before the transaction
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Write handlers can declare a beforeTransaction phase, and file bytes can be uploaded before the transaction
  detail: defineWriteHandler accepts beforeTransaction(event, ctx), which the dispatcher runs after the pre-handler gates and any reserveBeforeTransaction and before the transaction opens, so a slow external call holds no pool connection. Its data reaches the handler as event.prepared; a failure result or throw rejects the write, and its release runs whenever the transaction does not commit. ctx.write, appendEvent, notify and the other write surfaces throw inside the phase, and a handler with the phase cannot run as a nested ctx.write. uploadFileBytesBeforeTransaction writes the bytes in that phase and createFileRefFromUploadedBytes creates the fileRef row in the handler; the release keeps the bytes when the row exists. Original files whose row never committed stay in storage, no job sweeps them.
  -->
- 6b1567e: CapExceededError carries resetAt and retryAfterSeconds, API sets Retry-After
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-counter
  type: breaking
  title: CapExceededError carries resetAt and retryAfterSeconds, API sets Retry-After
  migration: |
    Periodic caps no longer need RateLimitError({ windowSeconds: 0, ... }). Where you catch CapExceededError from enforceCap and rethrow it as RateLimitError, drop the catch and let CapExceededError pass: the response stays 429 with a correct Retry-After, error.code becomes cap_exceeded instead of rate_limited, and error.details carries resetAt and retryAfterSeconds. Keep a feature-specific message with enforceCap({ ..., i18nKey }) and pass a period end other than the calendar month with periodEndIso (e.g. a budget's resetsAtIso). Clients matching on rate_limited for these caps must also accept cap_exceeded. Any KumikoError with retryAfterSeconds (including RateLimitError thrown in a handler) now gets a Retry-After header from /api/write, /api/batch and /api/query.
  -->
- dfb2523: Agent guide and generated indexes ship in the framework package
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Agent guide and generated indexes ship in the framework package
  detail: The framework package now contains AGENTS.md plus an agents/ directory with generated feature, widget and example indexes, built from feature-manifest.json, the renderer-web exports and samples/recipes. The new agent-docs-drift guard in kumiko check fails when the committed files differ from the generator output. New apps get an AGENTS.md and a CLAUDE.md that point at the packaged guide.
  -->
- 8fb6aa6: Handler field references support business keys and array fields
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Handler field references support business keys and array fields
  migration: |
    handlerFieldReference(schema, field) now returns { entity, by, multiple } instead of the entity string. Replace reference with reference.entity; skip or handle fields where by is set (value is a business key, not an id) or multiple is true (value is an array).
  -->
- f1b4367: Writes without an open transaction run as their own command
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Writes without an open transaction run as their own command; ctx.db writes there throw
  detail: Write handlers accept transaction "perCommand". Such a handler runs without a transaction of its own, so every ctx.write and ctx.writeAs it issues runs as its own top-level command with its own transaction, gates and afterCommit hooks. A perCommand handler cannot run as a nested ctx.write, cannot be part of a multi-command batch (422 per_command_handler_in_batch) and cannot combine with beforeTransaction or reserveBeforeTransaction (boot error). ctx.write and ctx.writeAs from stream handlers and top-level query handlers now take the same route, so afterCommit hooks of the called write, which never fired before, fire now. ctx.db writes (entity executor, insertOne, updateMany, deleteMany, db.global() writes) and event appends (appendEvent, unsafeAppendEvent, tryAppendEvent, fetchForWriting, archiveStream, restoreStream, snapshotAggregate) throw in stream handlers, top-level query handlers, perCommand handlers and in beforeTransaction and reserveBeforeTransaction. ctx.dbOutsideTransaction and ctx.outsideTransaction stay available, and ctx.db.unsafeRaw stays open as the audited escape hatch.
  migration: Stream and query code that writes through ctx.db or an executor bound to ctx.db calls a write handler through ctx.write or ctx.writeAs instead, or writes deliberately through ctx.dbOutsideTransaction. Check code that relied on afterCommit hooks of a write called from a stream or query handler not firing. bookCapUsage from a stream or query handler needs outsideTransaction true or a command. runInOwnTransaction(ctx.db, ...) stays locked in these contexts; runInOwnTransaction(ctx.dbOutsideTransaction, ...) is the way to a deliberate own transaction. Measured consumers: one stream handler (AI agent turn: conversation, activity and tool-call records through an executor on ctx.db, plus cap booking) and one query handler (AI text run: cap booking on ctx.db, log via ctx.write). No other consumer app has stream or query writes. The beforeTransaction/reserveBeforeTransaction lock affects no released code.
  -->
- b5a6395: templateVariable.richText declares a notification variable that carries sanitized HTML
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: improvement
  title: templateVariable.richText for notification variables that carry formatted HTML
  detail: Notification variables are escaped, so a value holding HTML (for example a document written in a rich text editor) showed up as literal tags in the mail. A variable declared with templateVariable.richText({ required }) is run through the document sanitizer at render time and inserted as HTML; bold, italic, lists and safe links stay, script, event handlers and javascript links are not emitted as markup. If the sanitizer rejects a value, it is rendered as escaped text and a warning with the violation codes is logged. All other variable types stay escaped.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 8e81d73: A throwing command in a batch without a database connection releases its cap reservation
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: A throwing command in a batch without a database connection releases its cap reservation
  detail: The sequential fallback of dispatchBatch (no DB connection) did not release the reserved capacity when a command threw instead of returning a failure result. It now releases the reservation before rethrowing.
  -->
- cfbffba: Boot-validator and guard messages say how to fix the problem
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Boot-validator and guard messages name the fix
  detail: Boot-validator and guard messages that only described the problem now also say what to do about it. The German configEdit and retention messages are in English. Validation and guard behavior is unchanged.
  -->
- 15039ce: Bootstrap idempotency for encrypted config and demoted invitations
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: fix
  title: Bootstrap reruns no longer rewrite encrypted config or restore dropped global roles
  detail: Declarative bootstrap compares encrypted and piiEncrypted config keys by their decrypted value, so a matching rerun writes nothing, and re-issues an invitation whose stored global roles are no longer in the plan. makeDispatchWriteAs is exported from the framework api.
  -->
- 8e81d73: CacheSyncBus.publish accepts remoteOnly to skip local listeners
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: CacheSyncBus.publish takes { remoteOnly } to skip same-process listeners
  detail: `publish(topic, message, { remoteOnly: true })` delivers only to other processes. Use it when the publisher has already applied the change locally and a local fanout would trigger a redundant reload.
  -->
- 2b255c2: Published changelog no longer names paths in private repositories
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: changes.json no longer ships paths into private repositories
  detail: Older changelog entries named file paths and a docs path of private repositories. They now name only the repository. The changelog guard rejects a `<private-repo>/<path>` reference or a github.com link into a private repository.
  -->
- 8e81d73: Config key validators get a db scoped to the tenant being written
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: config
  type: fix
  title: Config key validate() receives a db scoped to the written tenant
  detail: A SystemAdmin writing a config value for another tenant previously handed the validator a system-mode db that could read every tenant. `ConfigValidateContext.db` is now a `TenantDb` locked to the tenant the value is written for. The validator runs inside the write transaction, so a slow query there should set its own timeout.
  -->
- 8be3807: coerceRow takes a raw driver row and returns the caller's row type
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: coerceRow no longer claims the raw driver row already has the converted shape
  detail: coerceRow now accepts a Record<string, unknown> driver row and returns the explicitly requested row type, with the single cast at that boundary. The raw event-consumer, pending-event and projection-rebuild queries return untyped rows instead of a caller-chosen generic. The eventMigrations JSDoc and the expand/contract guide now state that pii and encrypted fields reach transforms as field-bound ciphertext and must not be renamed or derived from.
  -->
- 8e81d73: collectTableMetas rejects two features registering the same table name
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: collectTableMetas rejects two features registering the same table name
  detail: Two entities or storeTables with the same table name produced duplicate metas that only failed later in `schema generate` with a message about a hand-added meta. collectTableMetas now throws at the first registration with both origins, so setupTestStack fails the same way. The duplicate-name error of the migration generator no longer assumes a hand-added meta.
  -->
- 15039ce: System-cron escape hatch audits are deduplicated per target and repeat daily
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: System-cron escape hatch audits are deduplicated per target and repeat daily
  detail: The per-process dedup of declared system-cron hatches keyed only on handler, kind and tenant, so a run writing several global tables was audited for the first table only, and a worker running longer than the audit retention left no event. The key now includes the target and the process audits again after 24 hours.
  -->
- fd5009a: Entity detail cache hits with an ownership clause use one statement
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: A detail() cache hit with an ownership predicate costs one database statement
  detail: The ownership re-check and the live stream-version read for a cached detail row now run as a single query, so a cache hit is no more expensive than a cache miss for entities with SQL ownership rules.
  -->
- fd5009a: Login and logout expire leftover __Host- session cookies when the names resolve unprefixed
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: A later cookieDomain or secureCookies:false no longer leaves stale __Host- auth and csrf cookies behind
  detail: expireLegacySessionCookieVariants covers both directions. With unprefixed names and secure cookies, setAuthCookies and clearSessionCookies now also expire __Host-kumiko_auth and __Host-kumiko_csrf as Secure, Path=/, host-only. Before, the browser kept sending the stale __Host-kumiko_csrf in X-CSRF-Token and every write failed with csrf_token_mismatch until it expired.
  -->
- 8e81d73: Expired fileRef purge no longer stalls on rows that keep failing
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Expired fileRef purge no longer stalls on rows that keep failing
  detail: The soft-delete cleanup always selected the oldest 500 expired fileRefs, so 500 permanently failing rows (unsafe key, missing list permission) blocked every newer expired fileRef of that tenant. A run now walks the expired rows page by page along (deletedAt, id) and ends on an empty page; failed rows are retried on the next run.
  -->
- 15039ce: Extra routes outside /api get the request body cap for every entry
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Extra routes outside /api get the request body cap for every entry
  detail: extraRoutes with entry anonymous or user outside /api now run behind the maxRequestBytes body limit like signature routes already did, so an unauthenticated caller can no longer stream an oversized body into a public form or callback route.
  -->
- 8e81d73: FileContext.refFromFileRef reads files whose fileRef moved to another tenant
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: FileContext.refFromFileRef reads files whose fileRef moved to another tenant
  detail: A tenant handover moves the fileRef row but not the bytes, so the storageKey keeps the previous tenant's prefix and the tenant-bound `ctx.files.ref(key)` rejected it. FileContext gains `refFromFileRef({ storageKey })` for keys read from a fileRef row the caller has already tenant-checked: it skips the tenant-prefix check and still rejects unsafe keys. The variant route and ctx.derivatives.variant use it, so variants of handed-over files render again. `ref(key)` keeps the prefix check for freely supplied keys.
  -->
- 8e81d73: A save with file fields loads its fileRef rows once
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: A save with file fields loads its fileRef rows once
  detail: The tenant check and the pending-upload binding of a save each read every named fileRef row inside the write transaction. They now share one query over the ids, restricted to the writer's tenant and live rows. Values that are not UUIDs are still skipped.
  -->
- 7482ee2: Termination receipt limit no longer keys Redis by an unkeyed email hash
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: billing-foundation
  type: fix
  title: The termination receipt rate limit keys Redis with a keyed, handler-bound digest instead of an unkeyed SHA-256 of the email
  detail: HandlerContext gains an optional rateLimitDigest(value), an HMAC bound to the running handler, so a handler can build rate-limit keys without plaintext identifiers and cannot reproduce the dispatcher's payload-bucket digests. normalizePayloadBucketValue is exported from the pipeline entry point. The receipt limit reuses it, and withholds the receipt mail (the declaration is still recorded) when no digest is wired. Payload-bucket normalization now applies Unicode NFKC first, so fullwidth lookalikes share a bucket. Existing receipt buckets restart empty; they expire after the 24 hour window.
  -->
- 8e81d73: An empty jsonText match list no longer returns every row
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: An empty jsonText match list no longer returns every row
  detail: A where filter `{ jsonText: [] }` on a jsonb column used to add no condition, so the query returned all rows. It now matches no rows, like `in: []`. A `null` or non-object entry in the list throws the descriptive jsonText error instead of a bare TypeError.
  -->
- 5a39305: ListFacetSpec docs state that reference facets are exempt from the declared-column rule
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Facet field docs name the reference exception
  detail: The docs of projectionList.facets and relatedList.facets said every facet field must be a declared column. A facet of type "reference" is exempt: it filters by id through the bound query's filters and needs a registered entity instead. Behavior is unchanged.
  -->
- 8e81d73: list() reads rows and stream versions in one statement
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: list() reads rows and stream versions in one statement
  detail: The entity list read the rows first and the stream versions in a second statement, so a concurrent write could pair old row data with a newer version, and an update built on that version would pass the optimistic lock. The stream version is now a correlated subquery of the list statement, the same way detail() reads it.
  -->
- fd5009a: Meilisearch adapter re-applies the default index config when it gained fields
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Existing tenant indexes pick up searchable fields added to the registry default
  detail: The lazy default configuration now also applies to an index whose stored searchable, filterable and sortable attributes are a strict subset of the current default (an older default after a deploy added fields). Indexes holding any attribute outside the current default are treated as an explicit configure() and stay untouched, as before.
  -->
- fd5009a: Read paths decrypt file-reference fields again so legacy PII ciphertext does not leak
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: decryptForRead and eager-loaded refs decrypt file, image, files and images fields that hold legacy ciphertext
  detail: Only the encrypt side skips file-reference fields. The decrypt side uses collectPiiSubjectFields again and passes plaintext through unchanged, so rows written by the old backfill, which encrypted the file uuid, are read as plaintext instead of failing with pii_ciphertext_leak.
  -->
- 15039ce: Cascade deletes honour the record-lock exemptions and ignore soft-deleted children
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Cascade deletes honour the record-lock exemptions and ignore soft-deleted children
  detail: The cascade hook blocked a parent delete on a locked child even when the executor delete had skipped the lock guard (unsafeSkipLockGuard, a framework system write with a writePurpose, forget). DeleteContext now carries lockGuardBypassed and the hook follows it. Soft-deleted children no longer count as locked.
  -->
- 22f40e1: Reservation contexts reject transaction-bound writes
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: reserveBeforeTransaction contexts now reject writes that would escape the transaction
  detail: The context passed to reserveBeforeTransaction now throws on ctx.write, writeAs, event appends, scheduleAfterCommit, notify and jobRunner, like the beforeTransaction phase does. dbOutsideTransaction, outsideTransaction and forTenant stay available because reservations deliberately write outside the transaction.
  -->
- 5a2bea5: Restore re-encrypts PII in the restored event's previous snapshot
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Restore no longer writes plaintext PII from pre-KMS rows into the event log
  detail: Restore now decrypts the soft-deleted row and re-encrypts it like delete before storing previous, so rows written before the subject KMS was configured no longer leak plaintext personal fields into the restored event. Restoring such a row for an erased subject now fails like delete.
  -->
- 7482ee2: bindReferencedFiles loads file refs in bulk and skips refs it must not bind
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: bindReferencedFiles binds only refs of the record's tenant in one bulk load
  detail: File refs for a page are loaded with a single query restricted to the writer's tenant and live rows; system-owned refs are not bound to records.
  -->
- 7482ee2: Boot validator rejects more invalid screen and handler declarations
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Boot validator covers option, prefill, emptyState, anonymous rate-limit and searchable-access gaps
  detail: Rejects optionsQuery combined with optionsAvailabilityQuery, invalid dashboard valueFormat kinds, from-today panels without ranges or brush, params on emptyState navigate/drawer, unknown submitPrefilled keys, per-user rate limits on tenantless anonymous handlers, unknown conditional select option values, and searchable fields (including embedded sub-fields) the reader cannot access.
  -->
- 7482ee2: Dispatch routes validate requestId and every batch command up front
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Malformed requestId or batch command shapes return 400 instead of failing later
  detail: The dispatch and batch routes parse requestId and each command before dispatching, returning a validation error for malformed shapes, and the JSON body reader no longer relies on a type assertion.
  -->
- 7482ee2: Payload rate limits can normalize emails and auth requests use a 15-minute window
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: fix
  title: Email payload buckets ignore plus-tags and case; auth requests are capped at 3 per 15 minutes
  detail: additionalRateLimits accepts normalize: email, which lowercases and strips the plus-tag before hashing, and bucket keys are scoped by tenant and handler. Signup and token requests (reset, unlock, verification) and the waitlist default use it with a 3-request, 900-second window.
  -->
- 7482ee2: files and images fields enforce maxCount in the write schema
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: files/images maxCount is validated on write
  detail: The generated write schema applies .max(maxCount) to files and images fields, so payloads with more ids than allowed are rejected with a validation error.
  -->
- 7482ee2: Feature AST rendering drops an empty writeRoles list on secrets
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: render/parse roundtrip keeps secrets valid when writeRoles is empty
  detail: renderSecret and renderSecretNamespace omit writeRoles when the list is empty so the rendered source parses back to the same definition.
  -->
- 15039ce: A stale auth cookie on the SSE stream ends the web session with a session-ended frame
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: A stale auth cookie on the SSE stream ends the web session with a session-ended frame
  detail: With anonymousAccess, a stale or revoked auth cookie downgrades /api/sse to an anonymous 200, so the web client never noticed the session end and live updates stopped silently. The stream now opens with a session-ended frame carrying the rejection code and expires the auth cookies; the renderer-web live-events client calls onSessionEnded once for it.
  -->
- fd5009a: Tenant job run state is keyed by tenant, job name and BullMQ job id
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: jobs
  type: fix
  title: Tenant-visible job runs no longer collide across tenants, jobs and lanes
  detail: store_tenant_job_runs was unique on bull_job_id alone, but BullMQ ids count per queue, so a job on the api lane and one on the worker lane (or two tenants after a Redis reset) shared an id and overwrote each other's row. The unique index now covers (tenant_id, job_name, bull_job_id), every write filters by all three, and an enqueue replaces a finished row left over under the same key. onJobDropped now receives { tenantId } as a third argument.
  migration: |
    Run `kumiko-schema generate` in your app to add the migration that creates store_tenant_job_runs_tenant_job_bull_job_id_unique and drops store_tenant_job_runs_bull_job_id_unique (generated as a commented DROP INDEX; uncomment it). A custom onJobDropped callback passed to the job runner now gets a third argument { tenantId }.
  -->
- 55f003d: Test isolation for the search payload warn spy and the mail editor placeholder rail
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Unit tests no longer leak a console.warn spy into later files
  detail: The search payload precedence tests spy on console.warn per test and restore it, so later files in the same --no-isolate worker start with the real console.warn. The mail editor missing-language test waits for the placeholder rail instead of reading it before the validate query settled.
  -->
- fd5009a: transaction() on a transaction handle throws a clear InternalError
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Calling transaction() on a tx or savepoint handle fails with an InternalError
  detail: `RawClient.begin` is now typed optional, and `transaction()` checks it like `runInNewTransaction` does, so a nested call raises an InternalError ("runner has no begin()") instead of a TypeError. The migrate runner requires `begin` on its client and rejects handles without it before running any SQL.
  -->
- 8e81d73: Workflow failure logs show the original error
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: workflow-runner
  type: fix
  title: Workflow run-failed and retry logs carry the original cause
  detail: The ops log used to print the generic `workflow step N failed` wrapper. It now prints the underlying error, while the persisted event still carries the error class only.
  -->

## 0.363.0

### Minor Changes

- 58452ae: ctx.notify in write handlers delivers after commit

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: ctx.notify in write handlers delivers after commit
  detail: Inside a write handler's transaction ctx.notify only records the notification and delivers it once the write has committed, so a rolled-back write sends nothing and leaves no attempt event. Delivery no longer takes a connection from the app pool while the write holds one, which deadlocked at pool max N with N parallel writes. With immediate: true the call stays synchronous and runs its DB work on the outside-transaction pool.
  migration: |
    NotifyResult is now a union, NotifyDispatched ({ kind: "dispatched", deliveries }) or NotifyDeferred ({ kind: "deferred" }). In a write handler without immediate: true ctx.notify returns deferred and delivers after commit (a rollback means no notification). Code that reads the result (for example a "send test message" handler showing sent/failed) sets immediate: true, which delivers synchronously on the outside-transaction pool and returns dispatched; narrow on kind before reading deliveries. Errors such as a missing idempotency Redis, a tenant broadcast without the tenant feature or an unknown notification type no longer throw in a deferred write handler, they land in the afterCommit log. Notifications from jobs, from seeding and from handlers without a transaction stay synchronous. The boot default wires tenantUserIdsQuery for to: { tenant } when the tenant feature is mounted, so an app-side tenantUserIdsQuery wiring can go. Custom NotifyFactory implementations receive an optional 4th parameter deliveryDb, and DeliveryService.notify an optional 6th.
  -->

- fcd6eb4: Shared type guards and fewer unchecked casts in framework internals

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Shared type guards and fewer unchecked casts in framework internals
  detail: "@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/type-guards" exports isPlainObject, isOneOf and errorCodeOf. The framework replaces many unchecked as-casts with narrowing, generic query rows and table-introspection helpers. encryptPiiFieldValues is generic over the row and returns PiiEncryptedRow<TRow>, so callers read encrypted fields without casts. Behavior stays the same.
  -->

- 2972bc2: r.notification declares variables, mail template text and meta

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: r.notification declares variables, template and meta; applyBootSeeds seeds them
  detail: r.notification accepts variables (typed with templateVariable.text, link, money, date and list), template (per locale body, document html) and meta (per locale subject and more). Boot validation requires a kebab-case name, a meta.<locale>.subject for every template locale and valid placeholder names. templateVariablesToZod turns the variables into a Zod schema. applyBootSeeds calls seedNotificationTemplates, which writes the text as system templates of kind mail and fails loudly when notifications declare a template but the template-resolver feature is not mounted.
  -->

- ef689d8: r.notification without trigger, localizedTemplate and mail locale helpers

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: r.notification works without trigger and ships localized templates
  detail: trigger, recipient and data are optional and must be declared together, a notification without trigger is sent explicitly through ctx.notify. localizedTemplate groups body and meta per locale and is mutually exclusive with template and meta. The variable names link, money and date are reserved for template helpers. ctx.notify validates the data against the declared variables and fails the write on a missing required variable. New exports are listMailLocales, hasMailTranslationKey, assertNotificationVariables and NotificationLocalizedTemplate.
  -->

- 4a748c3: ctx.notify rejects a broadcast to another tenant

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: ctx.notify rejects a broadcast to another tenant
  detail: A notify with to: { tenant } now throws an AccessDeniedError (reason notify_foreign_tenant_broadcast) unless the tenant is the caller's own, before any delivery work. In a write handler it fails synchronously instead of landing in the afterCommit log. Notifications fired from seed hooks during self-signup no longer use the app pool inside the signup transaction, which deadlocked at pool max N with N parallel signups; they deliver after commit. ctx.scheduleAfterCommit is now absent in query bridges and post-commit contexts, where hooks pushed to it never ran; callers that check for it (cache-sync announce, set-tenant-tier onAssigned, form-draft discard, seed hooks) now run inline there instead of being dropped.
  migration: |
    to: { tenant } must be the tenant of the caller (user.tenantId of the handler or job context), otherwise notify throws; in a write handler the throw is synchronous. Seed-hook notifications in the signup transaction run after commit and return { kind: "deferred" } (immediate: true runs synchronously on the outside-transaction pool, which cannot see rows the signup transaction has not committed yet, so a tenant broadcast there finds no new member). No known consumer broadcasts to a foreign tenant.
  -->

- cbed66e: Template resources (images) and mail attachments

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: breaking
  title: linkedResources is no longer a payload field of upsertSystem/upsertTenant; resourceUpload and resourceRemove manage it
  detail: Two steps - upload the image with POST /api/files (multipart, no entityType), then call template-resolver:write:resource-upload with { sourceFileRefId, templateId?, key? }. The handler re-encodes the caller's own unclaimed upload into a new file ref (width at most 1200 px) and links it into the template; resource-remove unlinks a key. upsertSystem and upsertTenant no longer accept linkedResources and leave the stored value untouched on update. The size cap is the system config key resource-max-bytes (default 2 MiB); a cap above the files route's maxUploadSize has no effect because the upload is rejected first. The source upload stays as an unclaimed file.
  migration: |
    Whoever sent linkedResources with upsertSystem or upsertTenant now uploads the image via POST /api/files (multipart, no entityType) and links it with template-resolver:write:resource-upload { sourceFileRefId, templateId, key }. Server-side seeding (seedSystemTemplate linkedResources) stays.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: Notification messages carry attachments (file refs and inline cid images)
  detail: RenderedMessage and the send job payload accept attachments as references (kind file or inline), never bytes. ChannelContext.readAttachment resolves them tenant-scoped at send time; createDeliveryService takes a new filesForTenant option for the inline fallback path.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: channel-email
  type: improvement
  title: Email channel sends file attachments and inline cid images
  detail: EmailMessage.attachments is sent through the SMTP transport (inline images with Content-ID). notify data.attachments with kind file entries are resolved through the file store; the PII guard rejects ciphertext file names.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: NotifyFactory takes an optional fileProviderResolver, so immediate and bootstrap mails can read attachments too
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: improvement
  title: Bundle import re-encodes its images like resource-upload; re-seeding keeps uploaded system resources
  detail: importBundle and importBundleSystem store each bundle resource through the same normalization as resource-upload (decoded format decides the content type, SVG and non-images are rejected, width at most 1200 px, resource-max-bytes applies), so an exported bundle carries the re-encoded bytes. seedSystemTemplate without linkedResources no longer resets the links of an existing row, so images a system admin uploaded survive the next boot. storeTemplateResource from the template-resolver barrel is the normalizing store; the raw byte variant is gone.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: fix
  title: Queued mails render with the tenant's config again
  detail: The delivery render and send jobs read the tenant config through ctx.configFor, which job contexts do not carry, so queued mails rendered without tenant name, locale, currency and branding. Both jobs now use ctx.config, which the job runner builds for the payload's tenant.
  -->

- 366d89f: Template validation query, layout kinds as structured html, bundle import/export, copy-locale and notification record mapping

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: breaking
  title: Tenant mail-layouts are structured html, pdf-layout and document-pdf are placeholder-validated
  detail: A new validate query dry-runs the write pipeline (used, unknown and missing placeholders, canSave, canPublish). document-pdf, pdf-layout and mail-layout now go through the same placeholder gate as mail; document-pdf and pdf-layout know the system placeholders page and pages. A tenant mail-layout is html with a data-content slot plus header, signature and footer regions that renderer-mail-html wraps in a fixed MJML frame; raw mjml (with {{{content}}} exactly once) is system-only. New handlers export-bundle, import-bundle, import-bundle-system and copy-locale move a template with its resource files between tenants and locales. r.notification accepts a record mapping from an entity row to the declared variables, validated at boot. publish and archive no longer touch system rows through a tenant-scoped SystemAdmin.
  migration: |
    Tenant mail-layout rows stored as mjml are ignored by the renderer, which falls back to the system layout; re-create them as html with a data-content slot. upsert-system answers with an extra validation field. seedSystemTemplate errors now read `<label> rejected: <code> (<detail>); ...`. Layout bodies without the content slot are rejected on write. `set` now runs the same gate for mail, document-pdf, pdf-layout and mail-layout rows and rejects unsanitized markup or publish issues, since saving publishes; the mail renderer also re-sanitizes stored tenant html layouts and falls back to the system layout when they fail. upsert-system and upsert-tenant no longer accept linkedResources (resources go through the resource upload; bundle import and copy-locale attach them). Unknown data-resource keys are a validate warning (resource_not_uploaded), not a write error.
  -->

The auth session now provides the user through the new `CurrentUserProvider` / `useOptionalCurrentUser()` renderer context, and `user:me` additionally returns `effectiveTimeZone`, the user's effective IANA zone (own setting, else tenant, else UTC); without a user zone the locale resolver's zone is used.

The title resolves `screen:<id>.view.title` first and falls back to `screen:<id>.title`. This is UI only: write protection still comes from access rules and handlers on the server.

- a3a51aa: An entity can declare `lockedWhen: FieldCondition`, for example `lockedWhen: { field: "status", eq: "closed" }`. The event-store executor refuses `update` and `delete` on a stored row whose state meets the condition, so generic CRUD, custom handlers (whatever they return), nested `ctx.write` and jobs running as a regular user are all covered. The write answers 409 `record_locked` (`errors.recordLocked`) and the transaction rolls back, so no event is written. The check reads the state before the write, so the write that sets the lock still passes. A row that lacks the condition field counts as locked. The check runs after the entity and field ownership checks and before the event append, so a caller without write rights sees `ownership_denied`, not 409. `forget` (Art. 17) never checks the lock. A write by the framework system user skips it only when the executor call names a `writePurpose` (`WritePurposes.retention` or `WritePurposes.erasure`, exported from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db`); retention cleanup, the user-data erasure hooks and tenant destroy set it, so statutory deletion and anonymisation reach locked rows. A system-user write without a purpose is rejected like any other. A server-code call site that must change a locked row on purpose passes `{ unsafeSkipLockGuard: true }` as an executor option; neither it nor `writePurpose` is ever read from a request payload. Boot rejects a condition on an unknown field, on a `personal` or `encrypted` field, and on any type other than text, longText, select, boolean, number or reference. An `entityEdit` screen without its own `readOnly` shows a locked record as a read-only view, so the condition is declared once; a record that lacks the lock field (for example no read right on it) is always shown as a view, like the server treats it; `screen.readOnly` adds a UI-only condition on top; either one shows the view. A parent delete with `onDelete: cascade` or `setNull` answers 409 for the parent when a child row is locked, instead of removing or detaching it with the parent; this check runs in the dispatch delete lifecycle, so a write handler that returns the result of a parent `forget` is held back by a locked cascade child too. Remaining limits: `restore` is not guarded (it brings back unchanged data), and a custom projection that reacts to a domain event from `ctx.appendEvent` can still change a locked row, because that bypasses the executor. An app-written erasure hook should use `forget`; one that deletes or anonymises a locked row with `delete` or `update` needs `writePurpose: WritePurposes.erasure` as the system user, or `unsafeSkipLockGuard` as a regular user.

  feature: types
  type: improvement
  title: EntityDefinition.lockedWhen and the executor options unsafeSkipLockGuard and writePurpose
  detail: lockedWhen is a FieldCondition evaluated against the stored row. update and delete on the EventStoreExecutor take unsafeSkipLockGuard to opt one call out, and writePurpose (WritePurposes.retention or erasure) lets the framework system user through. EntityEditScreenDefinition.readOnly is combined with the entity's lockedWhen (either shows the view).
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes

  type: improvement
  title: Locked records reject executor writes
  detail: The event-store executor checks entity.lockedWhen against the loaded row in update and delete and fails with RecordLockedError (409, code record_locked, i18n key errors.recordLocked); a missing condition field counts as locked. Create, restore, forget, framework-system-user writes that name a writePurpose and the write that sets the lock pass. validateBoot rejects a lockedWhen field that is unknown, personal, encrypted or not a plain scalar type.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer

- 99d1037: `POST /files` with an `entityId` now requires that the caller may write that record, checked before any byte is stored. The record must be readable (else 404 `not_found`), the entity's update handler, entity `access.write` and the file field's write access must allow the caller (else 403), and the record must not be locked by `lockedWhen` (else 409 `record_locked`). Before, any signed-in user of the tenant could attach files to any entityId, including records they could not read or that did not exist. An `entityId` without an `entityType` is rejected with 400 `missing_entity_type`. A custom `accessGuard` does not replace this check.

  Migration: apps that attach files to records the uploader may not update must grant the update right or upload without an `entityId` and bind on save. An entity without a generic `:update` handler rejects uploads that carry an `entityId`. Uploads that used `entityId` as a free slot without a stored record (as the files-post-processing sample did) must create the record first.

  type: breaking

  migration: Grant the uploader the entity's update right for records they attach files to, or upload without an entityId and bind the file on save. Entities without a generic :update handler no longer accept uploads with an entityId. Code that used entityId as a free slot without a stored record must create the record first.
  -->

- a3a51aa: Uploads that no record has claimed yet can only be read by their uploader and `privilegedRoles`. That covers pending uploads (an `entityType` but no `entityId` yet) and uploads without any `entityType`. Before, any user of the tenant could read another user's upload through `GET /files/:id`, `/meta`, `/download-url` and `/variant/:name`: pending uploads until a record claimed them, uploads without an `entityType` forever. The file routes answer 404 as for any denied file. A save also binds the caller's pending uploads on update, not only on create. On update, only the file ids the update names in its `changes` are bound, so `createFileRefFromBytes` with `attachTo` and no `entityId`, followed by an update that stores the id, now attaches the file. A file without `entityType` can never be bound to a record, so it stays private to its uploader.

Before, files without entityType were readable by the whole tenant and pending uploads until a record claimed them. bindPendingFileRefs now also runs for updates and binds the file ids named in the update's changes for file, image, files and images fields (same entityType and fieldName, entityId null, insertedById = caller), so createFileRefFromBytes with attachTo but no entityId plus a following update write attaches the file to the record.

Apps that set accessGuard keep their own decision. Code that reads another user's pending upload before the record is saved must bind the file first or run as the uploader. - a3a51aa: An update that removes or replaces an id in a `file`, `image`, `files` or `images` field now deletes the dropped fileRef, so readers of the record get 404 for it. Before, the fileRef stayed bound to the record and readable by everyone who could read it. The delete is the one `DELETE /files/:id` uses (soft delete; the soft-delete cleanup job removes the binary once the retention period is over), runs in the save's transaction and only touches fileRefs bound to exactly this record and field. Pending, shared or elsewhere-bound ids in the previous value are left alone. Deleting a whole record does not dispose its files in this step.

The binary is removed by the soft-delete cleanup job after retention, or by forget.
  -->

- 99d1037: The per-tenant soft-delete cleanup now removes the stored bytes of expired soft-deleted fileRefs, derivatives included, before it removes their rows. Before, the rows were deleted and the binaries stayed in storage. A row whose bytes could not be deleted, or that is processed without a file provider, stays and is retried by the next run.

- f2346e5: `primaryAction` on a projectionDetail screen names the header action that renders as the filled primary button; the boot validator rejects an id that is not a header action.

  `emptyState` on an entityList or projectionList defines the title, description and an optional action for an empty list, and `description` now also shows on searchable lists; a search or filter without matches shows its own "no entries match" text (`kumiko.list.empty.filtered`).

  `header.statusToneField` on a projectionDetail screen picks the `statusTones` entry from another record field, so a badge text like "Terminated on 31.03.2027" keeps its tone.

  A writeHandler `redirect` accepts `tab` to open a specific tab of a projectionDetail target.

  File and image fields render as a rectangular thumbnail (variant, then original, then placeholder) or the file name instead of an id, in read-only forms and in list cells; `{ format: "image" | "file" }` selects the same display for list columns.

  On narrow screens the status badge of a projectionDetail header moves into the page body so a long status stays readable, and the header keeps the edit pencil.

  In a flow layout an edit field with `span` takes a full row.

  Writes now reject file and image field values whose file id does not exist or does not belong to the writer's tenant, with a validation error on the field.

  File and image fields only request ids that are UUIDs and encode the id and variant in the URL path.

### Patch Changes

- 4bf01ba: File and image fields with a `personal` annotation are no longer encrypted under an active subject KMS. Before, creating such a row failed because the uuid column received a `kumiko-pii:` ciphertext. The annotation stays and still drives the hard delete of the binary on forget.

The column holds only the fileRef uuid; the binary is erased by the file-ref user-data hook.
  -->

- 7f32198: Personal fields now follow the row's current owner. When an update moves the owner (none to X, or X to Y), the update event carries the personal fields under the new owner's key, so forgetting the new owner erases them. A new backfill option moves older tenant-keyed values under their owner. The boot backfill uses it in its one full pass per fingerprint.

  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Personal fields are re-keyed to the new owner on owner change
  detail: On absent to X and X to Y, the executor writes the personal fields (personal: { of: ownerField }) of the row under the new owner's key into the update event, so the projection, a rebuild and every event from the transition on agree and only the current owner's forget decides erasure. As a result <entity>.updated changes can contain personal fields the caller did not send. X to absent keeps the values under X so the last owner's forget still erases them. The created event from before an owner existed stays tenant-keyed in the immutable log. The new backfill option rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields moves such tenant-keyed values under the owner the projection or payload names (never via whenAbsent, a projection row of another tenant is ignored, other tenants' keys are not touched, a forgotten owner yields the erased sentinel). The boot PII backfill passes it, and its fingerprint now includes a transform version, so each deployment runs one full pass and afterwards only catch-up passes near the cursor. A created event whose owner transition happens after that full pass is not rescanned and stays tenant-keyed until someone runs backfillEventPiiEncryption(db, registry, { resolveOwnerFromProjection: true, rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields: true }) followed by a projection rebuild, or the transform version is bumped.
  migration: No consumer code change. The boot backfill runs in the background (startPiiEventBackfillOnBoot, it does not block readiness, KUMIKO_SKIP_PII_BACKFILL=1 turns it off). On the first boot after the bump it does one full scan of kumiko_events and rebuilds the affected projections. Consumers reading updated.changes must not treat a personal field there as a user edit when the owner field changed in the same event.
  -->

- 91fc70e: kumiko-schema generate and validate now reject ENTITY_METAS that list a table twice. Before, the migration silently diffed only the last definition, so a new index landed in the snapshot without any CREATE INDEX SQL.

## 0.360.0

### Minor Changes

- cc46b78: Session cookies written Secure and without a Domain attribute now use the `__Host-` prefix: `__Host-kumiko_auth`, `__Host-kumiko_csrf` and `__Host-kumiko_tenant`. A browser only accepts such a cookie when it is Secure, Path=/ and host-only, so a sibling subdomain can no longer set or shadow it. With `auth.cookieDomain` or without Secure the plain names stay. The new auth option `secureCookies` forces the Secure flag (default: `NODE_ENV === "production"`); buildServer resolves it once.

  The base names and the naming rule live in `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/session-cookies` (`AUTH_COOKIE_BASE`, `CSRF_COOKIE_BASE`, `TENANT_COOKIE_BASE`, `sessionCookieName`, `resolveSessionCookieNames`). `readCsrfToken()` reads the prefixed csrf cookie first and falls back to the plain one.

  A request that carries the auth or the csrf cookie name twice is treated as having no session cookie (anonymous with `anonymousAccess`, otherwise 401) and the response expires every cookie variant, so a shadowed or stale duplicate can no longer pin a browser to the wrong session.

  The Origin guard now also runs without `allowedOrigins` when the app's public origin is known: the new auth option `publicOrigin`, which runProdApp fills from `auth.mail.baseUrl` and then from the `APP_BASE_URL` env. It admits that origin plus the request's own host. Without such a URL runProdApp warns at boot in production and keeps running.

Login deletes the legacy unprefixed host-only cookies, logout and deleteTenantCookie delete the prefixed and the legacy names. The server reads only the resolved names, so a request that carries only the legacy kumiko_auth is anonymous. AUTH_COOKIE_NAME, CSRF_COOKIE_NAME and TENANT_COOKIE_NAME are removed from the framework and dispatcher-live; the base names and sessionCookieName() are exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/session-cookies and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/api, getSessionCookies(c) returns the resolved names of a request. The testing package's CSRF_COOKIE_NAME stays and resolves to the unprefixed name (e2e servers run without Secure).

Replace imports of AUTH_COOKIE_NAME, CSRF_COOKIE_NAME and TENANT_COOKIE_NAME with AUTH_COOKIE_BASE, CSRF_COOKIE_BASE and TENANT_COOKIE_BASE plus sessionCookieName(); e2e helpers that imported CSRF_COOKIE_NAME from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-dispatcher-live import it from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/e2e instead (known: solon e2e/_helpers/api.ts and e2e/session-ended.spec.ts, kumiko-enterprise ai-agent-live-transcription.integration.test.ts uses AUTH_COOKIE_NAME).
